observations.programme_model_source_text: P226 will engage in a one-way Dual Language Bilingual Education model to develop bilingualism and biliteracy based on high proficiency levels in English and a partner language. ELL’s will be grouped according to their home language and the class will be taught by one teacher with a bilingual extension who will teach in two languages (Spanish and English) and is fluent in both languages. ELL's in this program will have multiple opportunities to interact with non-ELL's during recess, mealtimes, dismissal and the various whole school activities held throughout the school year. Initially, the DLBE instructional day will follow the 80/20 percent model, with 80% of instruction being given in the students partner language and 20% given in English, with the goal being a move towards a 50/50 model.

observations.programme_model_source_text: At 277Q, we implement a One-Way Dual Language Bilingual Education Program. This model serves students who share the same home language of Spanish. All our participants are English Language Learners (ELLs). Instruction is provided in both English and Spanish, with the goal of developing bilingualism and biliteracy. Since all students are ELLs with the same home language, they are integrated for 100% of the day. Language allocation is 50% English and 50% in Spanish.

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our Spanish and Mandarin Dual Language programs follow a self-contained and side-by-side rollercoaster model. The Mandarin Dual Language classes follow a self-contained model where one teacher teaches in both languages. The Spanish Dual Language Kindergarten and 1st grade classes follow a side-by-side model where there are two teachers (one teaches English, while the other teaches Spanish). Our Pre-K, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th grade Spanish Dual Language program follows a self-contained model where one teacher teaches in both languages. In Grades K--5, the Dual Language program follows a 50/50 model. In this model, students will receive instruction in the target language for 50% of the day, while the other 50% of instruction will be in English. 100% of English proficient students and MLLs/ELLs are integrated.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In the Dual language programs the classroom teachers teach core content in both languages. DBN: 01M020 School: P.S. 020 Anna Silver 164 of 216

observations.programme_model_source_text: Literacy instruction in our self-contained DLBE classrooms alternates from home language to English. The allocation of language arts instruction in DLBE classes is moving towards 50% ELA and 50% HLA home language instruction is implemented with instruction in the content areas. In our 7-period day, we work to implement English language instruction for 3 full periods, target language instruction (Spanish) for 3 full periods, and 1 period for lunch to achieve the 50/50 balance of the model. All ELL students are programmed into STARS according to CR Part 154 Regulations. STARS is updated on a regular basis for newly admitted and discharged students. The EDUR is reviewed to help ensure our programming is being entered correctly. Instruction across all content areas is expected to be 50% in the target language and 50% in English All Levels: 180 mins. minimum of Home Language Arts required per week.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Core content area are taught in English and Spanish. As follows: TBE - EN & EM: A minimum of two core content area to be taught in students home language (ex. Math, Science and/or Social Studies) TR & EX: A minimum of one core content area to be taught in students home language (ex. Math, Science and/or Social Studies) DLA - In the dual language program, the goal is that all content areas be taught in both English and Spanish 50:50. We are moving towards that model in a"Roller Coaster" program design. We are currently alternating the content area in Spanish. DBN: 10X046 School: P.S. 046 Edgar Allan Poe 166 of 226

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our DL programs serve both ELL students in need of English language development and English-proficient students who are interested in learning a second language. Both groups provide good linguistic role models for each other and, through their interactions, support language development in both languages. For the 2025-2026 school year, we will have a DL program in each grade Kindergarten-Fifth Grade. Our Dual Language programs are self-contained classes comprised of approximately 50% ELLs and 50% of monolingual students. observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school implements a 50/50 Two-Way Dual Language Bilingual Education model, where instruction is equally divided between English and Spanish. This model aims to develop bilingualism, biliteracy, and cross-cultural understanding among students. In this model, approximately 50% of students are English Language Learners (ELLs), and 50% are English-proficient students. This balanced composition fosters an environment where students learn from and with each other, promoting mutual respect and cultural appreciation. Instruction is delivered in both languages across all core content areas, ensuring that both ELLs and English- proficient students are integrated throughout the instructional day. This approach supports the development of proficiency in both English and Spanish for all students.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Core content area in Math, Social Studies and Science is taught in English and Spanish. Additionally, all participating students receive literacy instruction in English (ELA) and Spanish (HLA). DBN: 10X054 School: P.S./I.S. 54 174 of 229

observations.programme_model_source_text: P.S. 595 follows a Dual Language Program through a 50/50 alternating day model. Therefore, ENL instruction is provided during English instruction and instruction is differentiated based on student proficiency level and time allotments as per CR Part 154. All content and literacy instruction in English is delivered using ENL methodologies and all instruction is differentiated to support the linguistic and literacy diversity in the classrooms. All K-5 students receive literacy instruction and content instruction in the new language and the home language. Classrooms are comprised of heterogeneously mixed ELLs and Non-ELLs as peer language models are essential for the oral language development of al l students. Within our ICT dual language classrooms, instruction occurs in self-contained classrooms provided by one certified and highly qualified bilingual teacher. During ENL instruction, the bilingual teachers provide targeted and differentiated ENL strategies and scaffolds for ELLs to ensure language progression. Teachers plan for content and language objectives (the latter reflecting differentiation based on level of language proficiency and literacy data).
observations.subject_language_source_text: All subjects are taught in English and Spanish. DBN: 12X595 School: P.S. 595 148 of 207

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school implements the Self-Contained Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) model, in which the Dual Language Classroom includes a balanced ratio of approximately 50% English-proficient students and 50% English Language Learners (ELLs) whose home language is Spanish. This intentional composition ensures that students serve as linguistic models for one another, creating a collaborative, language-rich learning environment that promotes biliteracy, bilingualism, and cross-cultural understanding. In this model, English proficient students and ELLs are fully integrated throughout the entire instructional day, meaning they learn together in both languages rather than being separated by language proficiency level. Instruction is delivered in both English and Spanish, following a 50/50 model in which approximately 50% of instruction is conducted in English and 50% in Spanish across content areas. This balanced approach allows students to develop high levels of proficiency in both languages, while accessing rigorous academic content aligned with state standards. Dual Language teachers strategically plan and differentiate instruction to ensure that language objectives are embedded within content instruction, and that both English-dominant and Spanish-dominant students are supported in developing their second language through authentic academic tasks, cooperative learning, and scaffolded support. The ENL teacher also collaborates with classroom teachers to provide integrated ENL instruction, ensuring that ELLs meet both language and academic learning goals while remaining fully included in the classroom community. This integrated model fosters equity, access, and high expectations for all learners, and supports long-term academic success and cultural pride in both language groups.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Grades K-2 are taught Social Studies and Science in Spanish and ELA and Math in English. Grades 3-5 are taught ELA and Social Studies in English and Math and Science in Spanish. ***At our school, the language of instruction for core content areas in the Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program is strategically designed to ensure students develop strong academic skills in both English and Spanish, while also building cross-linguistic connections and cultural understanding. The distribution of content areas across languages varies by grade band to support developmental and linguistic progression. Grades K–2: Social Studies and Science are taught in Spanish, providing students, especially Spanish-dominant ELLs, with rich opportunities to develop academic vocabulary and content knowledge in their home language. English Language Arts (ELA) and Math are taught in English, allowing English-dominant students to access foundational literacy and numeracy in their stronger language while their peers simultaneously acquire academic English. This language allocation helps support early biliteracy development by grounding each group of students in both languages across meaningful academic content. Grades 3–5: DBN: 12X463 School: URBAN SCHOLARS COMMUNITY SCHOOL 146 of 197 English Language Arts (ELA) and Social Studies are taught in English, building on the reading and writing skills established in the early grades while strengthening students' ability to express complex ideas in English. Math and Science are taught in Spanish, providing continued opportunities for students to deepen their academic Spanish proficiency and use content-specific language in authentic, problem-solving contexts. DBN: 12X463 School: URBAN SCHOLARS COMMUNITY SCHOOL 147 of 197

observations.programme_model_source_text: ELLs receive ENL as part of the 50% of instructional time devoted to English instruction. The language-rich environment of the classes includes a substantial population of students who are already proficient in English, and who serve as models for the ELLs. The DL teachers differentiate instruction while the EPs receive English Language Arts. Students at the Entering and Emerging levels receive 360 minutes of ENL per week, while students at the Transitioning and Expanding levels receive 180 minutes of ENL per week and 180 minutes of ELA. Students at the Commanding level will receive 90 minutes of ENL within the ELA period. Materials used include the Into Reading curriculum and Amira program, AWARD Reading program, and classroom libraries. In addition, the ENL Teacher may pull out ELLs at the Entering level who need extra help. Home Language Arts (HLA) instruction takes place during the Spanish half of the week. Students receive at least 5 periods of Spanish HLA a week. Home Language Arts Materials used include classroom libraries, and Estrellitas in Kindergarten to Second Grade. We also use Ariba la Lectura to enhance the development of Spanish spelling patterns in Grades 2-5. To accommodate the recent influx of students, we have also had departmentalization models used to support the needs of our newcomers to ensure instruction in both Spanish and English. There is instructional time dedicated to helping students learn the English language.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In the Dual Language Program content area instruction is given in both languages. Math is primarily taught in English, with support from realia and hands-on math materials, but the students are also taught in Spanish with the Spanish version of Illustrative Math. Science and Social Studies are taught in both languages, using realia, pictures and experiential activities such as hands-on science activities, as well as online resources, text and trade books. allocations.source_passage: Our School » French Dual Language French Dual Language Bienvenue! The program was initiated by Francophone parents who wanted their children to learn in their native language and Anglophone parents who wanted their children to acquire a second language. At PS 133, these parents found a supportive learning community led by Principal Heather Foster-Mann, who welcomed parent and community participation to build a Dual-Language Program (DLP) that will enrich children of all backgrounds. The first DLP class began in 2011 with one kindergarten class. The following year, we expanded to two kindergarten classes in French and also began our first Spanish Dual-Language Program class. As these classes move up all the way to 5th grade, the Dual-Language Programs grows with them. Today the French DLP spans from Kindergarten to 5th grade, and the Spanish DLP from Pre-K to 5th grade. Why French? French is spoken throughout the world. One of the official languages of the United Nations, it is also an official language in 29 countries spanning the globe, including nations in Europe, North America, Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean. The Francophone world is rich in diversity, and children who participate in the Dual-Language Program at PS 133 may find themselves equally capable of communicating with peers in countries as diverse as Canada, Belgium, Haiti, Vietnam, and Rwanda. Structure Anglophone and Francophone children learn both their primary and a secondary language in an immersion environment. Following a 50/50 model, 50% of the students are Anglophone and 50% Francophone, and half the daily instruction for students will be in French and the other half in English. How to ApplyApplications open early in the calendar year for the forthcoming school year. Dual-Language Testing Request: Please use the link below to request an appointment to have your child tested for Francophone seats in our Dual Language Program. You will receive an appointment confirmation via email from [email protected] within a few days of your request. For admissions information about the French Dual-Language Program at PS 133, please contact Parent Coordinator Ahmed Dickerson at [email protected] or (347) 563-5321.

Each class is delivered DL instruction for the full course of the day by 1 teacher. Instruction is taught daily 50% in English and 50% in Spanish. Students within the classes are of mixed proficiency level. Instruction is designed so that both languages support each content area. Academic vocabulary and skills are taught with the use of visuals such as pictures and charts, read alouds, groupwork and assessments. The DLBE program aims to develop bilingualism and biliteracy for both ELLs and English-proficient students by providing instruction in both English and the partner language (e.g., Spanish). Students receive instruction in both languages, typically on an alternating schedule (e.g., one day in English, the next in the partner language). This program model groups students heterogeneously, allowing ELLs and native English speakers to learn from each other and develop language skills in a collaborative environment. The DLBE program ensures that students maintain and develop their home language while acquiring English, fostering a balanced bilingual and bicultural education. observations.programme_model_source_text: The dual language model implemented at P.S. 59 is a two-way Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program, in which classes consist of a balanced combination of English proficient students and English Language Learners (ELLs). Our dual language teachers, who are certified in both common branches and hold a bilingual extension, deliver instruction in both the home language (Spanish) and the target language (English), supporting biliteracy and content learning across both languages. Instruction is delivered in a 50/50 model, meaning English proficient students and ELLs are integrated for 100% of the instructional day, with the languages of instruction alternating by subject or day depending on grade level and unit focus. The instructional minutes for ENL services are delivered through an integrated co-teaching model and vary based on NYSESLAT proficiency levels: Entering/Emerging: 360 minutes per week of integrated ENL/ELA instruction (1.5 hours daily), plus at least two bilingual content area subjects. Transitioning: 180 minutes per week of integrated ENL/ELA instruction, alongside home language arts and bilingual content instruction. Expanding: 180 minutes per week of integrated ENL/ELA support, as well as instruction in home language arts and bilingual content areas. Commanding: 90 minutes per week of continued ENL support via .5 integrated ENL/ELA or participation in language production projects, per NYSED guidelines for two-year post-commanding monitoring. All ENL services are scheduled and tracked in STARS Admin by our STARS administrator to ensure compliance with mandated minutes and instructional models.
observations.subject_language_source_text: For the 2025–2026 school year, students in our Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program receive instruction in both English and Spanish across core content areas. In alignment with CR Part 154 requirements, Entering and Emerging ELLs receive a minimum of two bilingual content area subjects, specifically Math and either Science or Social Studies, taught in the home language (Spanish) in addition to English Language Arts and Spanish Language Arts. This ensures full access to content while supporting the development of biliteracy. DBN: 14K059 School: P.S. 059 The Dawn Best School 157 of 205

Expanding: 180 minutes per week of integrated ENL/ELA support, as well as instruction in home language arts and bilingual content areas. Commanding: 90 minutes per week of continued ENL support via .5 integrated ENL/ELA or participation in language production projects, per NYSED guidelines for two-year post-commanding monitoring. All ENL services are scheduled and tracked in STARS Admin by our STARS administrator to ensure compliance with mandated minutes and instructional models.   For the 2025–2026 school year, students in our Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program receive instruction in both English and Spanish across core content areas. In alignment with CR Part 154 requirements, Entering and Emerging ELLs receive a minimum of two bilingual content area subjects, specifically Math and either Science or Social Studies, taught in the home language (Spanish) in addition to English Language Arts and Spanish Language Arts. This ensures full access to content while supporting the development of biliteracy. DBN: 14K059 School: P.S. 059 The Dawn Best School 157 of 205

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our French dual language program is a two-way DLBE model that uses both the side-by-side model and the self- contained model, depending on if we have two classes on a given grade or one class on a given grade based on student enrollment. For the 2025-2026 school year, we have two side-by-side classes in K, 1, and 2 while we have 1 self-contained bilingual French class in grade 3. In the case of the side-by-side models, the language of instruction alternates on a daily basis. Students go between their English and French teachers, receiving instruction in one language for a full day before switching to the other language of instruction the next day. In our self-contained classes, half of the day is in English, while the other half of the day is in French. In 4th and 5th grade, students receive one period of French instruction per day. In all cases, English proficient students and ELLs are integrated 100% of the day, except for when ELLs are pulled out for stand-alone ENL services.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In grades K-3, reading, writing, math, science and social studies are taught both in English and French. In Grades 4 and 5, students learn core subjects in their homerooms with French and non-French program students. French is only used during one period of stand alone French instruction each day. DBN: 14K110 School: P.S. 110 The Monitor 146 of 181

On days when Spanish is taught, English proficient students and ELL students are integrated for 100 % of the instructional day. On days when English is being taught, ELL students at the entering and emerging levels receive ENL stand-alone services in ELA and integrated ENL in ELA and Science content areas. Students at the Transitional level of language proficiency in the DBLE program receive .5 unit of integrated ENL in ELA and Science and .5 unit of stand alone ENL instruction with the ENL teacher. observations.programme_model_source_text: Dual Language Model: Self- Contained Dual Language Self Contain Classes Dual Language Programs For the school year 2025-2026, we will continue our dual language programs as a one-way enrichment dual language program, meaning enrollments of both Hispanic-American and Chinese- American heritages with a mix of English and Spanish or Chinese proficiency is present among the student population. The idea of an “enrichment-based program” is to bring these students together to teach each other the curriculum through their two heritage languages. (Collier, V. P., & Thomas, W. P. (2004).) In addition, the use of an enrichment based program is to create cognitive challenges through thematic units, with no translation and no repeated lessons in the other language, but instead building upon the understanding of skills and foundations of their L1 language to help their L2 language. Studies have evidenced that these types of programs that focus on real world problem solving stimulate students to make more than one year’s progress every year in both languages.(Collier, V. P., & Thomas, W. P. (2004). The goal of our programs align directly to district 15’s goal of having students learn how to speak, read, understand, and write in two languages, and also learn about and appreciate others’ cultures. (NYC Department of Education - District 15 Superintendent, 2022) For our K-5 classes we will be following a week by week language instruction schedule meaning; Week 1’s content instruction will be in English and week 2’s content instruction will be in home language with the exception of Social Emotional Learning, Heggerty, Phonological & Phonemic awareness, Vocabulary center in Grades 3-5 , and part of the writing component in the literacy blocks (K-2) and the full writing block in grades 3-5 . These subjects will always be taught in English in both weeks. We follow the weekly model at our school, one week in the home language, and one week in the new language. observations.programme_model_source_text: Spanish Dual Language Program at 15K124 The Spanish Dual Language program at 15K124 follows a self-contained model from kindergarten through fifth grade. Students in these classes are heterogeneously grouped, with mixed language proficiency levels determined by data collected from conferences, student work, and formal assessments. Bilingual teachers utilize the Policy and Reference Guide for Multilingual Learners/ELLs to determine the required units of study for each student. English Language Learners (ELLs) receive all or part of their mandated English as a New Language (ENL) instruction through an integrated co-teaching model, combining core content instruction with English language development. The program maintains a 100% integrated model, with English Proficient (EP) students and ELLs learning side by side in both English and Spanish. Literacy instruction is delivered in both languages during the literacy block. Mathematics and Science are taught in English, with native language support available to assist entering ELLs. Phonics, read-alouds, shared reading, interactive writing, and Social Studies are taught in Spanish, the target language. Additionally, 15K124 implements the Heggerty Spanish Phonemic and Phonological Awareness curriculum across all Spanish Dual Language classes in grades K–5, supporting early literacy development in Spanish.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Home Language Arts (HLA) is taught in Spanish, while all other core content areas are delivered in English. The Spanish Dual Language program follows a self-contained model from kindergarten through fifth grade, with 100% integration of English Proficient students and English Language Learners (ELLs). Instruction is designed to promote bilingualism and biliteracy through purposeful use of both English and Spanish. Curriculum and Language Allocation: Literacy (English and Spanish): Core Spanish literacy instruction is based on ¡Arriba la Lectura! (Grades K–5). All Spanish Dual Language classrooms implement the Heggerty Phonemic and Phonological Awareness curriculum in Spanish. Content Areas: English: Mathematics and Science Spanish: Word Study, Read Alouds, Shared Reading, Interactive Writing, and Social Studies This language allocation ensures balanced exposure to both languages, supporting students' academic development and linguistic growth in both English and Spanish. DBN: 15K124 School: P.S. 124 Silas B. Dutcher 166 of 239

observations.programme_model_source_text: At P.S. 169, we implement a Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program that is designed to meet the needs of both English Language Learners (ELLs) and English proficient students. The model is structured based on the needs of our students and their language proficiency levels. 1. Chinese Dual Language Program: In kindergarten, we might have a combination of self-contained and Dual Language Collaborative Integrated Co- Teaching (DLCH ICT) models. One kindergarten class is self-contained, while the other follows the ICT model, where ENL and bilingual educators work alongside the general education teacher. For grades 1-5, most of the Chinese Dual Language classes follow the side-by-side model. However, due to student enrollment numbers, one of our 5th-grade Chinese Dual Language classes is self-contained. 2. Spanish Dual Language Program: In the Spanish Dual Language program, we primarily follow the side-by-side model for most classes. Some classes, based on student enrollment and proficiency levels, are self-contained, where both content instruction and language instruction are delivered in the target language. 3. Integration of English Proficient Students and ELLs: In all of our Dual Language program models, English proficient students and ELLs are integrated throughout the entire instructional day. This integration happens as follows: – On English-language days, English proficient students serve as language models for the ELLs, helping to guide their language development. – On target-language days (Chinese or Spanish), ELLs serve as models to English proficient students in the target language. To further support language acquisition and academic growth, students are grouped based on specific learning needs. Small group instruction is provided to students, regardless of their English proficiency level, whenever there is a need to focus on a particular skill. Teachers, including our English and ESOL-certified teachers, work together to plan lessons that reflect the Universal Design for Learning (UDL) framework. This ensures that all students, regardless of language proficiency, have access to differentiated instruction and support that meets their unique learning needs. In this way, we foster an inclusive and supportive learning environment, where both English proficient students and ELLs have ample opportunities to develop language skills and content knowledge in both English and their home language.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In our Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program, core content areas are taught in both English and the target language (Chinese or Spanish). Instruction is split evenly, with 50% of the time spent in each language. This balanced approach ensures that students develop both academic content knowledge and language proficiency in both languages, fostering biliteracy and bilingualism. DBN: 15K169 School: P.S. 169 Sunset Park 154 of 252

observations.programme_model_source_text: For the dual language programs we follow a 50/50 model; with 50% of the instruction taught in English and 50% of instruction taught in the target language (Spanish). Dually certified instructors provide both ELA and HLA instructional minutes as per the "language of the day/period/unit/module." We use student proficiency levels to determine groups and number of minutes per week. For example, a student with the entering proficiency level will receive one unit of study in ENL stand-alone and one unit of study in ENL/ELA integrated in the classroom per week. Within small groupings (for both integrated and stand-alone minutes), ENL teachers ensure that mandated minutes of ENL service align with current CR Part 154 unit of study mandates. ENL and DLBE instructional minutes are provided according to the language proficiency levels as mandated by current CR Part 154 mandates. We use EDAT reports, screener data and in class assessments to guide our decisions.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Regardless of specific planning per grade and content demand, both the L1 and L2 are prioritized at having an equal 50% of instructional implementation. When considering grade level and academic demand, content is taught in both languages but the method of language delivery may vary. For example, lower and middle grades may follow a two week/10 day cycle that alternates between the two languages to best facilitate language and content learning, or upper grades may alternate languages by whole modules/units. Ultimately, each language is still given 50% of teaching time when considering the entire school year. DBN: 15K516 School: Sunset Park Avenues Elementary School 140 of 192

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school implements the self-contained model. This model is designed to provide a balanced and comprehensive approach to language instruction for both English proficient students and ELLs. Students switch between languages on a weekly basis. One week will focus entirely on English, and the next week will focus on the partner language(Chinese or Spanish). This model allows students to fully immerse themselves in each language for a week, fostering deeper understanding and language acquisition. It also helps to maintain a balance between the two languages over the course of the school year. Both English proficient students and ELLs work together, promoting peer support and interaction, which enhances language learning for all students. Dual Language Class flow of the day Grades K-2 Flow of the Day: Week 1: Instruction in English Social Emotional Learning (SEL): 15 minutes Read Aloud 20 minutes Phonics (Heggerty&Fundations) 35 minutes HMH Small Group/Differentiated work/Literacy Centers 20 minutes HMH Into Reading: 45 minutes Writing: 45 minutes Mathematics: 45 minutes PBL 45 minutes Enrichment/Cluster: 45minutes Week 2: Instruction in Home Language Phonics in English(Heggerty&Fundations) 35 minutes HMH small group/Differentiated work/Literacy centers in English (20 minutes) Social Emotional Learning/Read Aloud in Home Language: 20 minutes Home Language Arts/Small group/centers in home language 20 minutes HMH into reading: 45 minutes Writing : 45 minutes Mathematics: 45 minutes PBL 45 minutes Enrichment/Cluster: 45 minutes Grades 3-5 Flow of the Day: Week 1: Instruction in English Social Emotional Learning (SEL): 10 minutes Grammar: 20 minutes Math Routine 15 minutes Mathematics: 45 minutes Read aloud (20 mins) HMH Into Reading DBN: 15K896 School: The School of Creativity and Innovation 150 of 201 Engaging with Complex texts (35 mins) HMH Small Groups (35 mins) *Vocabulary Comprehension *Fluency *Building Knowledge *Guided reading Writing/Small Group 45 minutes PBL 45minutes Enrichment/Cluster: 45 minutes Week 2: Instruction in home language Social Emotional Learning (SEL) in English: 10 minutes Grammar in English : 20 minutes Math Routine 15 minutes in English Read aloud (20 mins) in home language HMH Into Reading in home language Engaging with Complex texts (35 mins) HMH Small Groups (35 mins) *Vocabulary Comprehension *Fluency *Building Knowledge *Guided reading Writing in home language 45 minutes Mathematics: 45 minutes in home language PBL 45 minutes in home language Enrichment/Cluster: 45 minutes in English By systematically planning instructional minutes, integrating ENL strategies, and monitoring student progress, the school’s Dual Language Alternate Week Model effectively meets the CR Part 154 ENL minutes requirements. This structured approach ensures that all ELLs receive the necessary language support to thrive academically.

observations.programme_model_source_text: Self-Contained model is implemented following a roller coaster model. 50% of the week will be allocated to English instruction and the remaining 50% is for Spanish instruction. A switch of language is done during 4th period or after lunch. Week A- Morning instruction is in English, Spanish instruction in the afternoons. Week B- Morning instruction in Spanish and Afternoons in English. Both English proficient students and ELLs are integrated throughout the entire day for all subjects. As much as possible, we will maintain a balance of 50/50 English-Language learners and English-proficient students integrated in the classroom. The ultimate goal is towards biliteracy and bilingualism in both English and Spanish.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In the lower grades, core contents are taught in both languages. In the upper grades (3-5) math and social studies and science are taught in English. DBN: 16K627 School: Brighter Choice Community School 168 of 199

observations.programme_model_source_text: PS 316 has a Two-Way Spanish-English DUAL Language Program in grades K-5. The Spanish-English Dual Language Program at P.S. 316 consists of one DL class per grade level in all grades, except for grade 3, which has two DL classrooms - one is GenEd Dual and one is Gifted and Talented Dual. Our Two-Way Dual program places both English-proficient/Spanish-learner students together with English-learner/Spanish-proficient students in the same classroom. Our dual classrooms are self-contained; all students stay in one classroom with two teachers – one who teaches ELA (English Language Arts) and the other who teaches SLA (Spanish Language Arts). The English- proficient students and the English-learner students are together the whole school day except when the ELLs leaves the dual classroom to go to the ENL classroom for stand-alone ENL instruction. The amount of time they are out of the classroom is determined by their English proficiency level. Entering and Emerging students have 180 minutes per week of stand-alone ENL. Transitioning students have 90 minutes per week of stand-alone ENL. Thus, the Entering and Emerging students are with the class 88% of the time and the Transitioning students are with the class 94% of the time. The Expanding and Commanding students are with their DL classes 100% of the time.
observations.subject_language_source_text: ELA is taught in English with home language support as needed for ELL students (Integrated ENL). SLA is taught in Spanish. Math is taught in English with English and Spanish materials and HL support for ML/ELLs. Social Studies and Science are taught in Spanish and English. DBN: 17K316 School: P.S. 316 Elijah Stroud 144 of 177

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our Dual Language program is a 70-30 general education program, with one Dual Language class per grade. Classes are mixed heterogeneously across proficiency levels. It is a two-way program in which a mix of both English Language Learners and English Proficient students are enrolled. ELLs and non-ELL students are integrated all day long. We use a whole group-small group teaching model where the teacher introduces a concept to the whole group and then breaks up the students into small groups according to needs and abilities. The groups are different for each content area subject and also change with frequency as the children grow and develop.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Science is taught in Spanish. Math is alternated every other day between Spanish and English. All other content areas are taught in both English and Spanish. DBN: 19K108 School: P.S. 108 Sal Abbracciamento 177 of 245

observations.programme_model_source_text: Dual Language Program In the Dual Language (Mandarin) classes they are integrated self contained models where classes provide full day instruction to students in needs of English language development alongside students who have are learning Mandarin and English is the home language. Half of the students' instruction is in English and students receive the other half of instruction in Mandarin. Instruction in Mandarin is taught through the content areas and literacy, such as ELA and Social Studies. In Kindergarten and first grade, the Dual Language programs are the side by side model. In grades 2-5 grade, the Dual Language programs are self-contained models. Grade 2-5 - the following academic supports have been provided: • Small group work in Level 1 and 2 for Phonics for Reading modified to support ENL learners by Bilingual/ ENL teachers Content area books and videos aligned to Wit and Wisdom modules, decodable texts, and appropriate reading levels are assigned to students. • iReady Learning Reading and Math where teachers can assign grade appropriate lessons and students work at their own pace and on their own grade level. (in Spanish) • Wit & Wisdom Staff Developers and District 2 Leads will continue to work with teachers to ensure Wit & Wisdom curriculum is taught with fidelity to support the instruction and to accommodate learning for all ENL students. • During lessons, videos and visuals are used to support lessons. • Students use chats, emails, Google Docs, Jam board, and Pear Deck to communicate, share ideas, and receive feedback.om Staff • Students use iChinese Reader to support lessons in Mandarin. Weekly family notices, memos, and newsletters (grades K-1) are sent home through translations, Class Dojo, or Google Translate.

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school has implemented a Two-Way Dual Language (TWDL) model, where students receive instruction in both Arabic and English. The school day is equally split between the two languages: 50% of the instructional day is conducted in Arabic 50% of the instructional day is conducted in English This balanced approach aims to foster biliteracy, bilingualism, and cross-cultural understanding for all students. It supports both native Arabic speakers and native English speakers in becoming proficient in both languages while mastering grade-level academic content. We are following the 50:50 model for grades K-5, using a "roller coaster" approach. Instruction alternates between Arabic and English daily, with lessons in one language in the morning and the other language in the afternoon. The next day, instruction continues in the language used the previous afternoon, with the switch occurring again in the afternoon. This structure ensures that students are exposed to both languages every day, enhancing their learning experience.
observations.subject_language_source_text: As of now, all content areas will be taught in both English and Arabic. DBN: 20K413 School: PS 413 135 of 175

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our dual language program is a Two-Way Dual Language Bilingual Education Program. In two-way DLBE programs, ELLs of the same language background and English proficient (EP) students, including native English speakers, learn content in two languages as they acquire the new language. In many instances, EP students, who may be former ELLs or heritage speakers, may also speak the partner language. This program is also referred to as “two-way immersion.” The goals of the two-way DLBE programs are for all multilingual learners, including ELLs, to develop bilingualism and biliteracy based on high proficiency levels in two languages, English and a partner language and achieve academically in both languages. ELL and EP students are integrated throughout the entire school day. The Language Allocation Program Model for our Dual Language Program is designed as 50:50 model.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Writing instruction and writing tasks allow for opportunities to use both English and Italian. Mathematics instruction is conducted in English with extension activities in Italian in order to build number sense and reasoning in both langauges. Social Studies and Art instruction is conducted in both Italian and English. Speaking and Listening is incorporated into all subject areas to meet grade level standards as well as develop language skills in both English and Italian. observations.programme_model_source_text: Our Dual Language program is a partial emergent program, or 50/50 program. The teachers teach fifty percent of the day in English and fifty percent of the day in Russian. In all of our DL classes English Proficient (EP) students and MLLs/ELLs are integrated 100% of the day and all content area subjects are taught together. We use monolingual lessons using the Rollercoaster model fostering knowledge across language, where Russian and English instruction alternate between morning and afternoon each day. In our DL program, all grades use the self-contained model, where the classroom teacher provides both English and Russian instruction as well as the ENL mandated services. In our DL program emergent literacy is taught simultaneously in both languages. Native Russian and English speaking children have the opportunity to develop their listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in both languages. observations.programme_model_source_text: P.S. 506 has Kindergarten - Fifth Grade Spanish Self-Contained 50-50 model Dual Language classrooms. The Dual Language (DL) program follows a model where English proficient students and ELLs of one common language (Spanish) learn together in two languages, English and the target language (Spanish). In our Dual Language classroom, students not only develop new language skills and learn academic subjects in both languages, they also practice and share language and culture with each other, making them bilingual, biliterate and bicultural. Our dual language programs offer students accessibility to high quality rigorous Next Generation Learning Standards (NGLS) aligned instruction that will prepare students for college and careers in the 21st century; as well as to be lifelong readers and writers. English proficient students and ELLs are integrated 100% of the day in our Dual Language self- contained classrooms.

Students also receive home language arts (HLA) instruction in Spanish for the mandated amount of minutes required during the reading and writing blocs. Phonics instruction is provided daily in English only in K-2 classrooms. All prep classes are in English only. The small group re-teach lesson bloc in literacy is in English. observations.programme_model_source_text: PS 69 uses the side-by-side side model for kindergarten. English and Mandarin instruction are taught 50/50. Dual language students learn 50% of the lessons in Mandarin Chinese across all subjects (reading, writing, math, social studies, etc.) and 50% of the lessons in all subjects in English. All core content areas are taught in both English and Mandarin. Emergent literacy is taught simultaneously. In kindergarten, we use the alternate day language model. There will be alternate full days in Chinese and English (students switch teachers/classrooms each day). Our school runs on a 7-day cycle. On Day 1, Class A would learn in the Chinese teacher’s classroom, and Class B would learn in the English teacher’s classroom. On Day 2, Class A would be with the English teacher, and Class B would be with the Chinese teacher. On Day 3, Class A would be back with the Chinese teacher, and Class B would be back with the English teacher; and so on.

observations.programme_model_source_text: In the Dual Language Program at P.S. 170, a side-by-side, two-way program model is used. One instructional day is taught in English; 100% of the day's instructional coursework is in English. Then, the next instructional day is taught in Mandarin and so on. Each core content area is taught in both English and Mandarin. Therefore, each language is separated by day. English proficient students and English language learners are equally integrated in the classes. 50% of the class' student population is EP and 50% of the class' student population is ELLs. Home language and English language literacy is taught simultaneously. Emergent literacy is developed in the home language and English according to the English language learner common core standards for language acquisition.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Each core content area is taught equally in both languages, Chinese and English. DBN: 20K170 School: Ralph A. Fabrizio School 158 of 224

observations.programme_model_source_text: This program was established during the 2017-18 school year. By 2022-23, all grades had one DL class with a dedicated Mandarin bilingual pedagogue. These classes follow a self-contained, two-way DLBE model. In a two-way dual bilingual program model, both English proficient students and English Language Learners (ELLs) are integrated for a significant portion of the instructional day. The goal of this model is to promote bilingualism, biliteracy, and multicultural competence for all students, regardless of their language background. Mandarin and English instruction is split over a 40:60 balance in K-1 and 30:70 in grades 2-5. The rollercoaster model is followed, meaning Mandarin instruction is conducted on Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings, as well as Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Literacy, Math, Science and Social Studies are all covered partially in Mandarin, and again in English during the allotted times. DBN: 21K101 School: P.S. 101 The Verrazano 135 of 207

observations.programme_model_source_text: There will be two Dual Language classes, second and fourth grade. Classes are a mixed ENL Spanish speakers and Spanish proficient speakers. The teachers use 50/50 model by alternating languages. The programs include ENL components. The ELLs in the Dual Language program will receive the mandated number of ENL instructional minutes as per CR Part 154: 360 minutes/week for entering and emerging ELLs, 180 minutes for transitional and expanding ELLs, and 90 minutes for Commanding former ELLs. The rationale of the program is to ensure all Dual Language learners, both EPs and ELLs to become bilingual, bi-literate, and bicultural so that they will meet the grade appropriate State Common Core and city educational standards.

observations.programme_model_source_text: We currently have a Russian dual language program that has grown from Kindergarten to fifth grade in a self- contained model. The program is a self-contained classroom that is one day in English and one day in Russian (50/50) in grades kindergarten to third grade. The class is made up of 50% of Russian native speaking ENL students, and 50% of non-ELL students. The program has grown into fifth grade in the 2022-23 school year. After the fifth grade class graduates and begins middle school, the students are integrated into the general education population. They will no longer be in a self-contained Russian dual language model. However, Russian language will be taught as a content area subject by a Russian language teacher.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Core Content area is taught in both English and Russian. In kindergarten, the program is implemented as such: reading, phonics, and writing is taught in English only. Shared reading, read alouds, social studies and some math is taught in Russian and English. In first grade to third grade, all content and literacy areas are taught in both English and Russian. In grades 4 and 5, students follow a departmentalized model. Some content areas are taught solely in English, while other subject areas are taught in Russian by a Russian dual language teacher. The current school year 2025-2026 services K-5 Russian Dual Language. We also offer Russian as a Foreign Language to Grades 6 and 7. Based on the 2024-25 monitoring for instruction and compliance, our school will implement a pilot program to strengthen our Dual Language program for the 2025-26 school year. DBN: 22K206 School: P.S. 206 Joseph F Lamb 143 of 209

observations.programme_model_source_text: Elm Tree Elementary School provides a Dual Language program using the 50/50 collaborative side by side model or stand-alone for grades PK through 5th. Research shows that students in a dual language program excel and show more progress than in other programs. The target language is Spanish being that most of our ELL/ML population's home language is Spanish. The students follow an alternating schedule and students in each class are heterogeneous with regards to proficiency levels. All classroom instruction will be provided in the 2 languages (L1 and L2) and time is evenly distributed for access and equity. Scaffolding will be provided for speaking, listening, reading, and writing activities by the teacher. We implement a two-way dual language program, which is based on the premise that two groups of students (each with different home languages, one being English) learn together in a systematic way so that both groups become bilingual and biliterate in the two languages. The benefits of this programming is language-minority students build their native language proficiency, which in the long run strengthens their acquisition of the majority language (English). English speakers develop proficiency in a new language, and their English skills are strengthened by this additional cognitive process.
observations.subject_language_source_text: For our Dual Language program literacy and math are taught in English and in Spanish on alternating days. Science/STEM and Social Studies are taught in English with home language supports utilized to facilitate language acquisition. DBN: 24Q211 School: Elm Tree Elementary School 165 of 260

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our self-contained, one-way dual language program serves students in grades K-5, with separate classes for Spanish Dual Language and Chinese Dual Language at each grade level. Each class is heterogeneously mixed, consisting of approximately 50% English Language Learners (ELLs) and 50% English Proficient (EP) students. In these classrooms, the language allocation for both content and literacy instruction is balanced, with approximately 50% of the instruction provided in English and 50% in the target language (either Spanish or Chinese). This balance is designed to promote bilingualism and biliteracy, ensuring that students develop proficiency in both languages while acquiring content knowledge. To meet the requirements of Part 154, ELLs receive the mandated English as a New Language (ENL) services required by CR Part 154.2, delivered by their certified bilingual teachers. These teachers also provide content-area instruction in both languages, supporting students' academic growth in subjects like Math, Science, Social Studies, and English Language Arts (ELA). In our dual language classrooms, students do not have separate language instruction time; instead, they are integrated for 100% of the instructional day, with English-proficient and native- language proficient students learning together. This integration ensures that all students benefit from peer-to-peer learning and develop language skills in both English and the target language. Instruction is designed so that content areas such as Math, Science, and Social Studies are taught using a 50/50 language distribution throughout a 5-day cycle. All dual language classrooms are equipped with instructional materials in both languages and are clearly organized using a color-coding system to designate the language of instruction—Red for the target language (Spanish or Chinese) and Blue for English. This system helps students and teachers easily identify which language is being used at any given time. By adhering to these practices, our program meets the guidelines of Part 154 for dual language instruction, ensuring that all students receive a high-quality, balanced education in both languages while supporting the development of academic and language skills.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In our dual language program, English and Chinese are taught in all core subject areas for the Chinese dual language classes, and English and Spanish are taught in all core subject areas for the Spanish dual language classes. The classroom teacher provides instruction in both languages across Math, Science, Social Studies, and English Language Arts (ELA). For Science, additional instruction is provided in English by a specialized science cluster teacher, ensuring that students receive content-specific support in English while maintaining the balance of bilingual instruction in the core subjects. DBN: 24Q007 School: P.S. 007 Louis F. Simeone 177 of 283

observations.programme_model_source_text: At PS 13 Q the self-contained model is followed for Dual Language Instruction. There is one Spanish/English two-way immersion class on each grade level in grades K through 5. There are three Mandarin/English two-way immersion classes: Grade K/1 Bridge, Grade 2/3 Bridge and Grade 4. The classes on each grade contain ELLs and English Proficient students. For each class, the teacher holds common branches and bilingual certification and speaks English and the heritage language. Instruction alternates daily between English and the heritage language, providing the foundation for the two-way immersion experience, and surpassing the minimum units of study requirement for integrated ENL and Home Language Arts. At PS 13, English proficient students and English Language Learners (ELLs) are fully integrated through the Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) programs. In each classroom, students from both groups learn together, benefiting from instruction that alternates daily between English and the heritage language—either Spanish or Mandarin. This two-way immersion model fosters bilingualism, biliteracy, and cultural understanding for all students. ELLs receive targeted support through both integrated and stand-alone ENL services, while English proficient students have the opportunity to develop and strengthen their heritage language skills. By learning alongside peers with diverse language backgrounds, students at PS 13 develop strong academic abilities and cultural competence, preparing them to succeed in multilingual and multicultural environments.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In both the Spanish and Mandarin Dual Language Programs at PS 13, core content areas such as math, social studies, and science are taught in both English and the heritage language, with instruction alternating daily to ensure a balanced 50/50 split between English and the partner language. Additionally, during the week, students receive instruction in science and social studies delivered in English by a cluster teacher, complementing the classroom teacher’s instruction of these subjects in both English and the heritage language. This structure supports students’ bilingual development while providing consistent exposure to rigorous academic content in both languages. DBN: 24Q013 School: P.S. 013 Clement C. Moore 138 of 228

observations.programme_model_source_text: At PS 13 Q the self-contained model is followed for Dual Language Instruction. There is one Spanish/English two-way immersion class on each grade level in grades K through 5. There are three Mandarin/English two-way immersion classes: Grade K/1 Bridge, Grade 2/3 Bridge and Grade 4. The classes on each grade contain ELLs and English Proficient students. For each class, the teacher holds common branches and bilingual certification and speaks English and the heritage language. Instruction alternates daily between English and the heritage language, providing the foundation for the two-way immersion experience, and surpassing the minimum units of study requirement for integrated ENL and Home Language Arts. At PS 13, English proficient students and English Language Learners (ELLs) are fully integrated through the Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) programs. In each classroom, students from both groups learn together, benefiting from instruction that alternates daily between English and the heritage language—either Spanish or Mandarin. This two-way immersion model fosters bilingualism, biliteracy, and cultural understanding for all students. ELLs receive targeted support through both integrated and stand-alone ENL services, while English proficient students have the opportunity to develop and strengthen their heritage language skills. By learning alongside peers with diverse language backgrounds, students at PS 13 develop strong academic abilities and cultural competence, preparing them to succeed in multilingual and multicultural environments.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In both the Spanish and Mandarin Dual Language Programs at PS 13, core content areas such as math, social studies, and science are taught in both English and the heritage language, with instruction alternating daily to ensure a balanced 50/50 split between English and the partner language. Additionally, during the week, students receive instruction in science and social studies delivered in English by a cluster teacher, complementing the classroom teacher’s instruction of these subjects in both English and the heritage language. This structure supports students’ bilingual development while providing consistent exposure to rigorous academic content in both languages. DBN: 24Q013 School: P.S. 013 Clement C. Moore 138 of 228

observations.programme_model_source_text: Dual Language Side-by-side: The side by side model is used only in Kindergarten within two classrooms and two teachers. Students are programmed according to their dominate language and are taught respective to the rotation and language of the room they are in that day. Using the HMH and Arriba La Lectura program, one teacher teaches a group of students in one classroom using both languages. The teacher switches between languages along with the students. This literacy instruction supports both English and native languages as evidenced within their schedules. Mathematics is also taught in both the primary and secondary languages by classroom teachers. A self-contained model is also used in grades K, 1, 4 and 5 following the noted program above.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Language Model: For the Dual Language Program the target language is used 35% of the time in grades 2-5 both EP and ELL students. The target language is used 50% of the time in Kindergarten and first grades. In Kindergarten Dual, language is separated by teacher and classroom for literacy and by subject for Science and Social Studies. In grade 3, language is separate by teacher and subject for Math and NLA. In grades 2, 4 and 5 language is separated by subject. Kindergarten ICT Dual Language classes use a self-contained model where language is separated by day and subject. Languages of Content: In grades 1-5 EP's and ELL are integrated 100% of the instructional day. In Kindergarten they are integrated for 60% of the school day. Literacy instruction is the only subject area that is taught separately for Kindergarten. DBN: 24Q019 School: P.S. 019 Marino Jeantet 168 of 243

observations.programme_model_source_text: At PS 88Q, we implement the 50/50 Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) model, which provides students with equal instructional time in both English and Spanish. Under this model, students spend approximately 50% of the instructional day learning in English and 50% in Spanish across all core content areas, including English Language Arts, Math, Science, and Social Studies. The classroom composition is intentionally balanced, with 50% of the students identifying Spanish as their home language (ELLs) and 50% identifying English as their primary language. This structure promotes full integration of English proficient students and ELLs throughout the entire school day, fostering bilingualism, biliteracy, and cross- cultural understanding. Instruction is delivered by a certified bilingual teacher, and the languages alternate daily to ensure consistent and equitable exposure to both English and Spanish.

observations.programme_model_source_text: At PS 110 the Dual Language model that is implemented is the side- by- side model. For kindergarten through fifth grade dual language classes, there are two teachers, each with their own classrooms: one English speaking and one Spanish speaking. The side-by-side model will be used to provide instruction to approximately 50 students between the two sections. Classes are composed of a mixture of English dominant and Spanish dominant students. MLs/ELLs are heterogeneously grouped; both classes contain students of various proficiency levels. MLs/ELLs receive ENL services from an ENL certified English language teacher (PiPo). Content areas are taught in both English and Spanish. English proficient students and MLs/ ELLs are integrated every day for the entire day for all subjects when the classroom teacher is ENL certified. If the classroom teacher is not ENL certified, an ENL certified teacher pushes in and therefore English proficient students and MLs/ELLs also remain integrated for the entire day for all subjects.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Students receive alternated days of language instruction in Spanish and English in the Dual Language program at P.S. 110. That is, every other day is a full day of instruction in one language, then the next day is a full day of instruction in the other language. Instruction is continuous and never repeated. In our TBE program, The TBE Language Allocation is expected to change as ML/ELL students acquire proficiency and are assessed by the teacher, utilizing formal and informal assessments, such as, Mclass in English and Spanish. In addition, other assessment tools, such as reading and writing rubrics, and unit assessments throughout the HMH modules will be used. * Entering = 25% English / 75% Spanish model is used * Emerging = 40% English /60% Spanish model is used * Transitioning = 50% English / 50% Spanish model is used * Expanding = 75% English / 25% Spanish model is used TBE content area breakdown- ELA & Social Studies- English Instruction Math/Science-Spanish instruction As students improve in language acquisition based on ongoing assessments, teachers in the TBE setting take this improvement into consideration in addition to the proficiency levels of students when planning, to incorporate the gradual release of language instruction within a lesson. This may be done via different parts of the lesson during the share, within a small group or during conferences as per student data. DBN: 24Q110 School: P.S. 110 139 of 239

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school implements the Two-Way Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) Program, also known as “two-way immersion.” In this model, English Language Learners (ELLs) who share the same home language and English Proficient (EP) students—including native English speakers, former ELLs, and heritage speakers—are integrated for instruction and learn academic content in both English and the partner language. In the Dual Language program, English Dual Language Teachers and ENL Providers collaborate to ensure that schedules are aligned to meet the mandated units of study in accordance to CR Part 154.2, based on students’ ML/ELL proficiency levels and program type. All Dual Language students receive bilingual content area instruction, in accordance with CR Part 154.2. For Dual Language programs, a 50/50 model is implemented. Students receive 50% of the yearly instruction in Spanish and 50% of the yearly instruction in English. Both literacy and content are taught equally in both Spanish and English over the course of the program. Instruction is delivered in one language at a time without translation. Our DL self-contained and DL ICT programs extends from grades K-5. In our Two-Way DLBE classrooms, English proficient students and ELLs are integrated for 100% of the instructional day. Instruction is delivered in both English and the partner language using a balanced model that supports language development and content mastery in both languages. This structure promotes collaboration and interaction among all students while supporting equity, inclusion, and academic excellence.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Core content area instruction is delivered in compliance with the legislative mandates and directives for each ML/ELL program as described in CR Part 154.2. The Transitional Bilingual Education teachers and Dual Language teachers align their instruction according to content units of study and the Next Generation Learning Standards (NGLS). Teachers utilize Language Objectives to provide all students with equal access to the curriculum as well. The teachers employ scaffolding strategies to enrich home language development in addition to English language development in all content areas. HMH Into Reading and Arriba la Lectura materials are utilized to support stages of language and literacy development for our diverse populations. The HMH Into Reading and Arriba la Lectura curricula enable students of varied proficiency levels to increase their reading and writing skills with the implementation of a variety of strategies. To develop Math skills in the home language and the English language, we construct our lessons by bringing the language of Math that our ML/ELLs encounter during their Envisions instruction. Dual Language (DL) program: In Dual Language classes, students receive 50% of the yearly instruction in the Spanish and 50% of the yearly instruction in English. Both literacy and content areas are taught equally in both Spanish and English over the course of the program. Instruction is delivered in one language at a time without translation. DBN: 24Q143 School: P.S. 143 Louis Armstrong 149 of 250 Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE): Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program: Currently we have 12 Dual Language General Education classes and 6 Dual Language ICT classes. Dual Language (DL) General Education Classes consist of two classes in each grade. Each class consists of one teacher who holds a Bilingual license. The Dual Language teachers employ a 50/50 model where Spanish and English instruction is delivered equally. Classes are grouped heterogeneously, consisting of ML/ELLs, FELLs, and Non-ELLs. Thus, the ML/ELL levels in the Dual Language classes range from Entering to Commanding. All ML/ELLs receive instruction for the mandated units of study according to their proficiency level by the classroom teachers. The classroom teacher integrates ENL strategies in the content area and, in addition, provides Stand-Alone ENL instruction for Entering and Emerging students. Non-ELLs are placed in this setting due to the fact that their parents have expressed a desire for their child to achieve proficiency in both languages. The Non-ELLs can be from Spanish speaking homes, or from homes where English or another language is spoken primarily. In this specific program, students are immersed in instruction that supports their home language and culture. Our Dual Language Integrated Co-Teaching (ICT) Classes consist of one class per grade ranging from grades K-5. Instruction will be delivered by a teacher who has a Special Education license, as well as a teacher who holds a Common Branch/Bilingual license. In some classes, one of the classroom teachers may also be TESOL certified. The teachers provide their ML/ELLs with the necessary strategies to meet students’ individual needs as well as Special Education students’ IEP goals. In addition, both teachers provide students with the mandated instructional minutes according to their ML/ELL proficiency level through a collaborative co-teaching approach. The classes consist of about 30 students, in which there is a maximum of 12 students with an Individualized Educational Plan (IEP) whose language of instruction is Spanish, according to their IEPs. The remainder of the class consists of a mixture of ELLs and Non-ELLs from Spanish speaking homes, or from homes where English or another language is spoken primarily. Students without IEPs are placed in this setting due to the fact that their parents have expressed a desire for their child to achieve proficiency in both languages. In this program, students are also immersed in instruction that supports their home language and culture. Grade appropriate leveled texts (English/Spanish to support home language) will be used to support discussion. In addition, writing stems/sentence frames will be used to engage students in conversation with family members. Additional supports include, visual aids, read alouds, videos, vocabulary; computer based instructional resources. To develop student's early literacy skills, mCLASS, Heggerty in English and Spanish and OG will be used. To aide students with comprehending grade appropriate skills, the curriculum HMH Into Reading and Arriba la Lectura (HMH Spanish) will be used in the classroom in grades K-5. observations.programme_model_source_text: The dual language model that is incorporated into P.S. 153 is the self-contained model. The environment of the classroom, including text and resources, reflects both languages. The children stay together all day in one classroom for all periods, including clusters. English proficient students and ELLs are integrated into 100% of the instructional day in this self-contained model as they are always learning together.
observations.subject_language_source_text: The core content areas are split 50/50 in terms of what language they are being taught in. The core content area is taught in that one language for the entire year. Reading and writing literacy skills are taught in both languages once in the morning and once in the afternoon, respectively. Mathematics is taught in Polish throughout the year, although vocabulary is introduced in both languages. This is done to support English proficient students and to create a bridge between the two languages where the languages meet. Social studies is taught in the English language. Science is taught in the Polish language. DBN: 24Q153 School: P.S. 153 Maspeth Elem 149 of 204

Students beginning in Kindergarten are placed in their classes, and an effort is made to have an even ratio of English proficient students and ELLs. At the culmination of each year, teachers are asked to look at their class compositions and make adjustments to the cohorts, if necessary. With two classes, side-by-side, each class is created in Kindergarten with a even split of English proficient students and ELLs.   In the side-by-side model, the content areas are taught in English and Spanish. DBN: 24Q016 School: P.S. Q016 The Nancy DeBenedittis School 165 of 242 Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE): Dual Language Program Students are grouped heterogeneously by mixed proficiency levels. Integrated and stand-alone ENL services are implemented in the English component of the Dual Language program. Students in each class alternate between Spanish and English on alternate days: for example, the 3-2 DL will begin week one with the English teacher on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays and the Spanish teacher on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The 3-3DL will begin week one with the Spanish teacher on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays and the English teacher on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The following week, the groups alternate. All ELL students in DL programs develop second-language skills while learning content knowledge in both languages. ELL students in the DL program receive ENL within the program itself. A small group instructional setting gives ELL students the mandated instructional time per their proficiency levels. All time allocations for Dual adhere to the outlined in NYS CR Part-154. The goal is for students to achieve proficiency in both languages, and it serves both English Language Learners and English-proficient students. Instruction is provided in English and Spanish, and a day is dedicated to each language. Teachers are fluent in both languages, and teaching is content-based, meaning students learn grade-level material. The group is often heterogeneous, mixing students with varying proficiency levels in both languages to promote language exchange and peer support. DBN: 24Q016 School: P.S. Q016 The Nancy DeBenedittis School 161 of 242 2. How does your school ensure the mandated number of instructional minutes are provided according to students’ English language proficiency levels in each program model? I have completed programming in STARS following the requirements according to CR Part 154. Teachers are provided with a copy of the CR Part 154 Requirements for ENL services and Transitional Bilingual Programs. Explicit ESL is delivered in each program as follows: Transitional Bilingual Programs: There are four Transitional Bilingual classes in grades K-5. Students in these classes are placed heterogeneously and grouped within the class according to their reading and native language arts abilities to meet individual needs. Academic instruction is in English and the native language, which, at P.S. 16, is Spanish. Classroom libraries consisting of children’s literature in Spanish, including fiction, poetry, and non-fiction books that appeal to various interests, are present. Our Transitional Bilingual program includes an ESL component for all students and requires more ESL instruction for students testing at benchmark levels 1 and 2. Transitional Bilingual students will continue to receive instruction in English in traditional enrichment or prep courses, such as Art, Computer Lab, and Physical Education. As students acquire English, the amount of academic instruction in English increases, which helps ensure they have the necessary skills to exit the program and succeed academically in English. Students starting with limited English spend 30 or 40 percent of their time in English language development, with instruction in the native language starting at 70 or 60 percent. As mandated by Regulation Part 154, advanced ELLs receive 180 minutes (4 periods per week) of instruction in Native Language Arts and 180 minutes (4 periods per week) of ESL instruction. Also, Entering and Emerging ELLs receive 360 minutes (8 periods per week) of ESL instruction and 180 minutes (4 periods per week) of Native Language Arts. observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school has scheduled a FLEX period every day for grades 3-5, and 3 times per week for grades K-2. Students are pulled for stand-alone ENL instruction during these periods as per CR-154. Additionally, students receive integrated minutes from ENL teachers that push-in during their ELA Reading and Writing periods. For Dual Language classes, the students split their time equally between their home language and English. For grades 5, we have a side-by-side model in which the students spend two full days per week in Mandarin, two full days per week in English, and Mondays are split between the two languages. For grades K-4, we have one class per grade, and the teacher alternates equally between English and Mandarin following the same model as the side by side structure: 2 days of English, 2 days of Mandarin, and Monday being split equally between the two languages.

observations.programme_model_source_text: A Dual Language model is implemented to allow students to master academic content to become bilingual, bi-literate and bicultural. The instruction is structured to implement approximately 50% of the instructional time to meet the needs of both languages (English and Mandarin/ English and Spanish). Teachers use a rollercoaster model. Language of instruction shifts within the same day. The morning begins with instruction in the home language and in the afternoon language of instruction is in English. The next day, the language of instruction in the morning is in English and it is in the home language in the afternoon. Opportunities for students to integrate language and content instruction is intentional and carefully planned with high academic expectations for all students. Both English proficient students and ELLs spend 50% of the instructional time learning in the target language (Chinese/Spanish) and 50% of the instruction in English. All ELLs are provided ongoing exposure to both languages and have access to standard aligned high-quality translated curriculum materials across the content areas.
observations.subject_language_source_text: All content area instruction for our dual language program are taught through alternating days between English and Mandarin/English and Spanish. DBN: 25Q021 School: P.S. 021 Edward Hart 155 of 240

The next day, the language of instruction in the morning is in English and it is in the home language in the afternoon. Opportunities for students to integrate language and content instruction is intentional and carefully planned with high academic expectations for all students. Both English proficient students and ELLs spend 50% of the instructional time learning in the target language (Chinese/Spanish) and 50% of the instruction in English. All ELLs are provided ongoing exposure to both languages and have access to standard aligned high-quality translated curriculum materials across the content areas.   All content area instruction for our dual language program are taught through alternating days between English and Mandarin/English and Spanish. DBN: 25Q021 School: P.S. 021 Edward Hart 155 of 240
