observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school offers a side-by-side Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program. 50% of the instructional day learning in English and 50% in the Mandarin. In this model, students are grouped into two classes: one receives instruction primarily in English, and the other in Mandarin. Both groups follow the same curriculum and learning standards, but each is taught in its designated language for specific content areas. Throughout the week, students from both groups interact and participate in joint activities, allowing them to practice both languages in academic and social contexts. Certified bilingual teachers coordinate closely to ensure that students in both classes are progressing in the same academic content and language skills. The side-by-side setup allows English Language Learners (ELLs) and English-proficient students to learn alongside one another, fostering bilingualism, biliteracy, and cultural understanding. Students are grouped heterogeneously by language background, so they serve as language models for each other and support each other’s development in both English and the partner language. This approach creates a balanced, inclusive environment where all students have equitable access to rigorous instruction in both languages.
observations.subject_language_source_text: English and Mandarin are the languages taught in each core content area. DBN: 25Q163 School: P.S. 163 Flushing Heights 148 of 215

observations.programme_model_source_text: The side by side model has been implemented in the Dual Language program since 2007. There are two teachers per class; one teaches English and the other teaches Chinese, with the exception of grades 2 & 5 who have dually certified in ESOL & Bilingual Extension, teaching both English and Chinese sections. The Dual Language program provides instruction in reading, writing, math, and social studies in English for 50% of the instructional time and in Chinese (Mandarin) for 50% of the instructional time. The students develop the content and concept knowledge in content areas in English and Chinese. On the days that the students are learning in English, the teacher provides small group instruction supporting English language development. The English and Chinese teachers serving the same grade meet regularly to discuss content and student progress. The Chinese teachers serving different grade levels also meet on a weekly basis to ensure students’ native language instruction is aligned across grades. Communication and collaboration are in effect during remote learning. In addition, ENL teachers provide integrated and standalone support and work with small groups based on their individual needs and mandated minutes of ENL services.

observations.programme_model_source_text: At our school, we implement a 50:50 Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) model in Spanish and English. In this model, students receive 50% of their instruction in English and 50% in Spanish across content areas such as literacy, math, social studies, and science. Student Integration: English proficient students and English Language Learners (ELLs) are fully integrated throughout the instructional day. They learn together in the same classroom environment, engaging with content and language objectives in both program languages. This integration fosters biliteracy, bilingualism, and cross-cultural competency, which are foundational goals of the DLBE model. Lessons are carefully planned to ensure that both language groups are supported and challenged, with intentional scaffolds, language objectives, and cultural representation embedded in daily instruction.

The resources used include HMH Into Reading/Arriba La Lectura, Amplify Math, Amplify Science, and Passports. Workbooks for Amplify Math are available in Spanish. observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school implements a Spanish Dual Language One-Way 50/50 model. This is a self-contained general education program with one dual language class per grade from Kindergarten through Grade 5. Classes are heterogeneously mixed across English Language Learners (ELLs) and English proficient students. This one-way model enrolls primarily Spanish-dominant ELLs alongside English-dominant students whose home language is Spanish. Throughout the instructional day, ELLs and non-ELLs are fully integrated and learn together. We use a combination of whole group and small group teaching models. The teacher introduces concepts to the entire class and then breaks students into smaller groups based on their individual needs and proficiency levels. These groups are flexible and change according to content area and language of instruction. Instruction is split evenly between the two languages, with a daily language rotation: Monday and Wednesday: Instruction is delivered in English Tuesday and Thursday: Instruction is delivered in Spanish Friday: Instruction is split half-day English and half-day Spanish This 50/50 instructional split ensures that students receive balanced exposure to both English and Spanish throughout the week, promoting bilingualism, biliteracy, and cross-cultural understanding. Our school utilizes a range of curricular resources and instructional absolutes to support Dual Language and ENL instruction. For literacy, we use Arriba La Lectura and Benchmark / Aprendo Leyendo for phonics and reading skills. I-ready spanish diagnostics. Math instruction is supported with Envision Matemáticas, and Spanish language learning is reinforced through Amplify. Estrellita is used in lower grades. In grades k-5 during small group time teachers utlize aprendo leyendo during Spanish phonics. In addition, Dual Language vertical teams collaborate regularly to ensure alignment of curriculum, instructional practices, and student supports across grade levels. These resources and structures help ensure consistent, high-quality instruction in both languages while addressing the needs of all learners on a weekly basis during common planning period.
observations.subject_language_source_text: On Monday and Wednesday ELA and Math are taught in English. On Tuesday and Thursday HLA and Math are taught in Spanish. On Friday ELA and Science are taught in English and Math and Social Studies are taught in Spanish. The language the content area is taught in is dependent on the language of instruction for the day. DBN: 28Q082 School: P.S. 082 Hammond 144 of 211

observations.programme_model_source_text: The Dual Language model that is implemented at P.S. 86 is self-contained. English proficient students and ELLS are integrated 100% of the instructional day. Instruction is provided by a Bilingual Licensed Teacher. The Entering students will receive 1 unit of study per week (180 minutes) done using the Integrated ENL model in ELA, Science, and/or Math. The Emerging students receive 1 unit of study in ENL/ELA (180 min.) using the Integrated ENL model. The Transitioning student will receive .5 units of study in Integrated ENL/ELA (90 minutes). The Expanding student will receive 1 unit of study per week (180 minutes), where 1 unit of study (180 min.) will be given in ENL/ELA or another Core Content Area using the Integrated ENL model. Commanding students, or former ELLs, receive .5 units of study in Integrated ENL/Core Content Areas for two additional years after proficiency level is attained. All ENL integrated or Stand Alone is aligned to the Four Modalities (Speaking, Listening, Reading, and Writing) and conducted during the ELA, Writing, Science, or Math core instructional times. We use the following curriculum: HMH Reading/Arriba la Lectura, Envisions Math, and Amplify Science. All data is discussed in our ILT, MTSS, and Vertical teams to dive into the data focusing on the ELL's. The ELL students are grouped on iReady to monitor progress and create targeted instruction to focus on skill gaps. K-2 also utilizes Acadience data to identify foundational skills to provide small group instruction through MTSS models and we do progress monitoring every 6 weeks.
observations.subject_language_source_text: The languages used to teach each core content area are English and Spanish. The students receive core instruction in English and Spanish using Envisions Math, Into Reading/Writing, and Amplify Science. DBN: 28Q086 School: P.S. Q086 139 of 208

observations.programme_model_source_text: The Dual Language Bilingual Education model implemented at P.S/I.S.116 uses a two-way roller-coaster model. This 50/50 model aims to develop bilingualism and biliteracy in both languages, enhance academic achievement, and cultivate cross- cultural understanding. English proficient students and Spanish proficient students (ELLs) are taught in both English and Spanish language provided the same day following a 50/50 roller coaster model. For example, on Monday morning instruction is in English and then it transitions to Spanish in the afternoon. The next day's instruction will start in Spanish in the morning and transitions to English in the afternoon. With this model both languages are targeted equally in each content area.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Each content area is taught in English and Spanish in the Dual Language program. DBN: 29Q116 School: P.S./I.S. 116 William C. Hughley 139 of 205

observations.programme_model_source_text: PS 75’s K-5 English and Spanish Dual Language Program follows the 50/50 language instruction model, and students receive instruction in both English and Spanish, with each language comprising approximately half (50%) of the instructional time. This DLBE program is aimed at fostering bilingualism, biliteracy, and cross-cultural competence among students. Dual Language classes are heterogeneously composed of English-proficient students and EL/MLLs, the students are integrated for the entirety of their school day in the classroom. Furthermore, when planning for small-group targeted instruction, english-proficient and EL/MLL students are grouped together based on their support needs. To provide comprehensive support, all out-of-classroom teachers collaborate closely with the classroom teacher in assisting ML/ELL students during specials, throughout the instructional day, our English- proficient students and emergent bilingual learners are integrated for the entirety of their learning time.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Core Content Areas: Reading, Writing, Math, Social Studies, and Phonics are taught in English and in Spanish. On Mondays and Wednesdays students receive instruction in Spanish. On Tusdays and Thursday’s students receive instruction in English. On Friday’s, students receive instruction in English half of the day, and in Spanish during the remaining half of the day. DBN: 03M075 School: P.S. 075 Emily Dickinson 143 of 204

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our dual language classes are self-contained with the goal of being comprised of 50% native English speakers and 50% native Spanish and Spanish proficient students. Currently, most classes are comprised of 33% native Spanish speakers, 33% bilingual Spanish speakers (heritage language speakers), and 34% native English speakers The school day is taught 50% in English and 50% in Spanish. Second language acquisition techniques are used during the day so both English dominant and Spanish dominant students are able to acquire a second language, thus becoming bilingual and bi-literate.

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school uses the 50/50 model for all Dual Language programs. For the school year 2025- 2026, we will have a Russian DL (PK-5) and Spanish DL program (PK-5). DL teachers will provide instruction in English 50% of the time and in the target language the remaining 50% of the time. In all our Dual Language classes, the English proficient students (EPs) and our ELLs are placed in heterogeneous groups to balance the language proficiency ratio throughout the day. The core content area is taught in both English and the Home Language. Language of instruction is separated and alternated daily. There is a target language calendar which we follow and is uploaded onto our Google Drive. The target language calendar is shared with parents and staff in the beginning of the school year on the school app. Emergent literacy is taught in both languages simultaneously.
observations.subject_language_source_text: The core content area is taught in both the English language with the target languages (Spanish and Russian) alternated daily. DBN: 03M145 School: P.S. 145, The Bloomingdale School 148 of 200

allocations.source_passage: Dual LanguageDual Language programs are important as they promote bilingualism and cultural diversity, allowing students to develop proficiency in multiple languages from an early age. ​ Our two Dual Language programs are one way that makes P.S. 145 unique. We follow an alternate day model within our Dual Language programs, where students receive instruction in English or in the target language (Spanish or Russian) depending on the day schedule.About the Russian ProgramДорогие друзья! Добро пожаловать в двуязычную программу 145 школы Блумингдейл. Меня зовут Оксана О'Шей . Я преподаю в пятом классе и работаю координатором русской программы. Удовлетворение академических и социальных потребностей учащихся посредством поочередного преподавания предметов на русском и английском языках является основной задачей обучения и воспитания в нашей школе. ​ Мы стремимся научить детей читать, писать, разговаривать и думать на русском и английском языках. Программа призвана обеспечить благоприятную академическую и эмоциональную среду для успешного развития потенциала учащихся. ​ Все педагоги, работающие в двуязычных классах, в совершенстве владеют английским и русским. Жизненный опыт, знание культурных традиций, доброта и терпение учителей делают нашу программу эффективной для учеников и важной для общины. ​ Мы постоянно расширяем школьную библиотеку новой литературой на русском языке. Учителя повышают квалификацию, перенимая опыт коллег и изучая новые технологии. ​ Если у Вас возникли вопросы о русскоязычной программе школы #145, пожалуйста, обращайтесь по электронной почте ooshea@schools.nyc.gov или oksana@ps145m.org.Welcome to the Russian Dual Language Program at P.S. 145, the Bloomingdale School! My name is Oksana O'Shea. I am a fifth-grade teacher and RDLP Coordinator at P.S. 145. The mission of our Dual Language program is meeting the academic and social needs of children by teaching them according to a 50/50 model: one day in English, the next in Russian. ​ The program is designed to provide a nurturing environment, prompting students to develop their potential to the fullest. Our goal is helping students become bilingual and biliterate in both languages. ​ All teachers working in the RDLP are fluent in English and Russian. Life experience, cultural knowledge, kindness and patience of faculty make our program effective for students and important for the community. As teachers, we are a community of learners ourselves. We are constantly expanding the school library with authentic literature in Russian. Teachers develop their professional skills by learning from colleagues and adopting new technologies. If you have any questions about RDLP at P.S. 145, please contact me at Ooshea@schools.nyc.gov or oksana@ps145m.org.About the Spanish Program ¡Bienvenidos! Mi nombre es Veronica Chan y estoy orgullosa de ser parte de la comunidad escolar de PS 145M como maestra y Coordinadora del Programa de Lenguaje Dual en Español. Nuestro Programa de Lenguaje Dual en Español es una piedra angular de nuestro enfoque educativo, atendiendo a estudiantes desde Pre-K hasta el 5º grado. ​ Nuestro programa está diseñado para proporcionar a los estudiantes un ambiente de aprendizaje acogedor donde puedan participar en experiencias de aprendizaje rigurosas, divertidas y prácticas. Nuestro objetivo final es ayudar a los estudiantes a convertirse en bilingües y alfabetizados en español e inglés. ​ Todos nuestros maestros del programa son completamente bilingües, aportando una gran cantidad de conocimiento y riqueza cultural a nuestras aulas. A lo largo de los años, hemos mejorado continuamente nuestros métodos de enseñanza y hemos reunido numerosos recursos multilingües de varios países de habla hispana. Estos recursos mejoran el aprendizaje de los estudiantes y les brindan una exposición significativa a su cultura de origen. ​ Nuestro programa de lenguaje dual ha sido una parte vibrante de nuestra comunidad y escuela durante muchos años, fomentando el amor por el aprendizaje y la apreciación cultural en nuestros estudiantes. Estoy emocionada de contribuir al éxito y crecimiento continuo de este programa. ​ No dudes en contactarme a vchan25@schools.nyc.gov o veronica.chan@ps145m.org. Welcome! My name is Veronica Chan, and I am proud to be a part of the P.S. 145M school community as both a teacher and the Spanish Dual Language Program Coordinator. Our Spanish Dual Language Program is a cornerstone of our educational approach, serving students from Pre-K through 5th grade. ​ Our program is designed to provide students with a nurturing learning environment where they can engage in rigorous, enjoyable, and hands-on learning experiences. Our ultimate goal is to help students become bilingual and biliterate in both Spanish and English. ​ All of our program teachers are fully bilingual, bringing a wealth of knowledge and cultural richness to our classrooms. Over the years, we have continuously improved our teaching methods and gathered numerous multilingual resources from various Spanish-speaking countries. These resources enhance student learning and provide meaningful exposure to their heritage culture. ​ Our Dual Language program has been a vibrant part of our community and school for many years, fostering a love for learning and cultural appreciation in our students. I am excited to contribute to the continued success and growth of this program. ​ Feel free to reach out to me at vchan25@schools.nyc.gov or veronica.chan@ps145m.org.

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school uses the 50/50 model for all Dual Language programs. For the school year 2025- 2026, we will have a Russian DL (PK-5) and Spanish DL program (PK-5). DL teachers will provide instruction in English 50% of the time and in the target language the remaining 50% of the time. In all our Dual Language classes, the English proficient students (EPs) and our ELLs are placed in heterogeneous groups to balance the language proficiency ratio throughout the day. The core content area is taught in both English and the Home Language. Language of instruction is separated and alternated daily. There is a target language calendar which we follow and is uploaded onto our Google Drive. The target language calendar is shared with parents and staff in the beginning of the school year on the school app. Emergent literacy is taught in both languages simultaneously.

observations.programme_model_source_text: PS163 Dual Language program is a One-Way (self-contained) model. In the Dual Language program, the targeted language is Spanish. The Dual Language program is designed to have students spend half of their instructional time with a target language of immersion. The remaining part of the week is spent with English-only instruction. In grades one through five, the school uses an alternating day model in which language used for content areas alternates from day to day (Monday through Thursday). Fridays are spent 50 percent in English, and 50 percent in Spanish. In Kindergarten, the model is 80 percent in Spanish and 20 percent in English. ELL students receive integrated and stand-alone ENL during English only days within the classroom when ELLs are grouped together. Within the classroom, bilingual teachers take ELLs aside (during stand-alone instruction) or scaffolds and differentiate ELA instruction (during integrated instruction). ELLs at the entering and emerging levels receive 360 minutes of ENL instruction per week within the classroom, ELLs at the transitioning and expanding levels receive 180 minutes per week of ENL instruction, and ELLs at the commanding level receive 90 minutes of ENL instruction per week. Furthermore, students in the Dual Language program receive ELA instruction for 108 minutes on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays during reading and writing workshop. The bilingual teachers use the ReadyGen curriculum for Reading and Writing Workshop. Furthermore, HLA is provided to students in our Dual Language program using the Biliteracy Pathways curriculum on alternating days. The curriculum provides ELL students with HLA instruction in reading and writing for 108 minutes per day on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays.

DBN: 30Q329 School: East Elmhurst Community School 147 of 215 Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE): DBN: 30Q329 School: East Elmhurst Community School 143 of 215 East Elmhurst Community School offers a one-way Dual Language (DL) class from Kindergarten to Fourth grade. Preference for the program is given to English Language Learners, since Dual is an ELL entitled program. The instruction is delivered in the roller coaster model, across ELA and all content areas. Both languages are provided equal space to be developed academically, using a weekly schedule - one week in English, one week in Spanish. Similar to the English as a New Language program, students in the Dual program will be able to have rich experiences and be supported according to their needs, in both languages. DBN: 30Q329 School: East Elmhurst Community School 144 of 215 2. How does your school ensure the mandated number of instructional minutes are provided according to students’ English language proficiency levels in each program model? More than a third of students at East Elmhurst Community School are classified as English Language Learners. However, nearly all of our students speak another language(s) - in addition to English - outside of school. As such, ENL methodology is paramount to all instructional work in our community in order to meet the needs of all language learners: preserve, and increase, English proficiency and the native language (in the Dual program). EECS believes in the inclusion and push-in services to support our students' language acquisition needs. ELLs receive support of English Language Arts, and Home Language instruction, via the classroom teacher with multiple certifications; or push-in support from a qualified/certified ENL teacher. Teachers work in grade team groups (and across grades) to develop meaningful lessons that incorporate the skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing. The school follows the mandated instructional minutes as per CR Part 154. Students receive mandated services according to their NYSESLAT or NYSITELL proficiency level. The school ensures the mandated instruction minutes are provided by following CR Part 154-2 Units of Study requirements for each of the ELL program models we offer - Dual and ENL. The ENL coordinator oversees that teachers are up-to-date with their NYS certification and that current, and former, ELLs are receiving mandated integrated and/or stand-alone ENL. 3. How are ENL, English Language Arts (ELA) and if applicable, Home Language Arts (HLA) instructional minutes delivered in each program model? ENL Program: East Elmhurst Community School has mixed ability classes where students acquire language skills and receive language support from one another. With classroom instruction delivered by dual certified teachers and push-in/pull-out support, students also benefit from small group instruction, pre-teaching and ESL methodologies. Some strategies used across all classes, with emphasis on our ELLs, are: 1) Pre-teaching vocabulary - Pre-teaching concepts in the L1 for easier transition into L2 (when necessary). 2) Break up text and activities into small, manageable chunks. 3) Provide visual word banks, sentence frames (sentence starts for Entering/Emerging ELLs) for written responses 2) Translanguaging, where students may produce in their L1 to reflect their receptive understanding of L2 content. Over time, they are able to produce more in the L2 without the L1 support. 3) Total Physical Response, where students and teachers use gestures, acting out, body/facial expressions and physical movements to reinforce communication in the L2. 4) Small group work, with explicit language skills embedded. 5) Access to the information/content in the L1 via texts and/or video. 6) Non-textual visuals with entry points for all language learners. observations.programme_model_source_text: We use a Two-Way Dual Language model at our school which means that two language groups of students will be joined in the same class to become bilingual, bicultural, and biliterate. Our dual language classes are composed of an equal number of Spanish-speaking and English-speaking students who are learning in both languages. The language of instruction is alternated daily by the teacher. This is called a "50/50 Roller Coaster Model." One day is taught in English and the next day Spanish. a. The time is split equally, 50/50 between Spanish and English (the target language). b. The entire instructional day is integrated with no content areas being taught separately. Students are strategically seated according to different language proficiency levels so that students can also serve as language models to each other. c. Language is separated daily and not by subject, teacher, or theme. Alternate language (English/Spanish), is used each day of the week. For example, "A Week" is: Monday: Spanish, Tuesday: English, Wednesday: Spanish, Thursday: English and Friday: Spanish (Spanish dominant week), while "B Week" is: Monday: English, Tuesday: Spanish, Wednesday: English, Thursday: Spanish, and Fridays: English (English dominant week). d. The Dual Language Model used is the self-contained, roller coaster model.

observations.programme_model_source_text: At PS 112, our DLBE program is implemented in a mixed mode format. Within the instructional day, 50% of the day is taught in English, and 50% is taught in Spanish. Typically, English instruction takes place in the morning, and Spanish instruction in the afternoon. The subjects being taught do not correspond to a specific language. The program card of the teacher determines which subjects will be taught in which language for the day. Each curriculum has a component in both English and Spanish. The curricula used is as follows: HMH Into Reading (English) and Arriba La Lectura (Spanish), Math uses Envisons (English and Spanish), Amplify Science (English/Spanish), Social Studies, Passport (English and Spanish), Estrellia (K-1 only), Heggerty (English/Spanish), and Fundations (English only).
observations.subject_language_source_text: English and Spanish. As mentioned, this varies based on the teacher's daily program card, and if the content area takes place in the morning (English instruction) or the afternoon (Spanish instruction). DBN: 30Q112 School: P.S. 112 Dutch Kills 160 of 223

observations.programme_model_source_text: At PS280Q, our Dual Language program 50% of instruction in is the target language and 50% of instruction is in the native language. In our school we use the alternate week model. EP's and ELLs are in a self contained dual language class. English-Proficient (EPs) and ELLs are integrated throughout the entire day. Core content area is taught in both English and Spanish during the alternating weeks. In our Dual language program, we currently use the alternate week model. Students are provided instruction in one language for one week and then in the other language the following week, alternating weekly. Instruction is not translated but builds upon the previous week. Teachers make explicit connections between the languages to ensure content understanding. Instruction is alternated between English and Spanish on a weekly basis, for example, one week is in English and the next week is in Spanish by a dually certified teacher (Common Branch/Bilingual Cert Extension). There are also several ways to structure classroom schedules effectively. Our schedule follows an A/B-week model. With this structure, students spend an entire week learning in one language, and the next week in the other language (Spanish). This offers continuity in one language for the entire week. At P.S.280Q we help motivate the students to integrate both languages by immersing them in reading, writing and speaking. We believe that reading books together, providing many different writing materials, keeping books, magazines, and newspapers around for children to access are all good ways to immerse children in the world of print. Core content area is taught in both English and Spanish during the alternating weeks. In our Dual language program, we currently use the alternate week model. Students are provided instruction in one language for one week and then in the other language the following week, alternating weekly. Instruction is not translated but builds upon the previous week. Teachers make explicit connections between the languages to ensure content understanding. Instruction is alternated between English and Spanish on a weekly basis, for example, one week is in English and the next week is in Spanish by a dually certified teacher (Common Branch/Bilingual Cert Extension). There are also several ways to structure classroom schedules effectively. Our schedule follows an A/B-week model. With this structure, students spend an entire week learning in one language, and the next week in the other language (Spanish). This offers continuity in one language for the entire week. At P.S.280Q we help motivate the students to integrate both languages by immersing them in reading, writing and speaking. observations.programme_model_source_text: The Dual Language model implemented at PS398Q is a two-way, self-contained program that follows the 50:50 model for grades K-3. Grades 4 and 5 dual language model is a two-way, departmentalize program that follows the 50:50 model where one certified bilingual teacher delivers instruction for Math and Science and the other for ELA and Social Studies. Our program is largely comprised of two groups, each coming from households where one of two languages, English or Spanish, is dominant. Our 50:50 dual language model alternates the language of instruction each day; all instruction is done in English one day and the next day all instruction is carried out in Spanish thus providing the 50/50 balance between languages. MLLs/ELLs in the program have the opportunity to continue developing students’ home languages, as well as English language skills. The program gives the opportunity to students who are English-proficient students to learn a new language and current Spanish-proficient students to become true bilinguals who gain academic proficiency in all modalities (Speaking, Listening, Reading and Writing) in both English and Spanish.

observations.programme_model_source_text: At P.S. 20, we implement a one-way Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) program model within Integrated Co- Teaching (ICT) classes. This model primarily serves English Language Learners (ELLs) who share the same home language (Spanish), though students may demonstrate varying levels of proficiency in both Spanish and English and come from diverse dialectal backgrounds. Instruction is delivered equally in English and Spanish, following a 50/50 model in which each language comprises approximately 50% of the instructional day. The goal is to develop bilingualism, biliteracy, and cross-cultural competence, while also ensuring access to rigorous academic content. In this model: English proficient students and ELLs are fully integrated for the entire instructional day. All students learn together in both languages, receiving content instruction, literacy instruction, and language development support in Spanish and English. This inclusive approach ensures that both English proficient students and ELLs benefit from rich, linguistically and culturally responsive instruction, while promoting equity and academic excellence for all learners.

observations.programme_model_source_text: At P.S. 44, we implement a self-contained Dual Language model. In our roller-coaster model, we provide 50% in English and 50 % in Spanish. English proficient students and MLLs/ELLs receive integrated Dual Language instruction as we have a self-contained model. In the self-contained model of dual language education, a single teacher instructs a group of students within a single classroom, providing instruction in both languages. This model contrasts with other dual language approaches where students might be pulled out for specialized instruction or rotate between different teachers. MLLs receive their ENL minutes within the 50% of English instruction in our self- contained Dual Language model. ENL students spend at least 85% of their time with English proficient students. The Dual Language teachers in Grades Kindergarten through 5th grade provide Integrated ENL instruction. The Dual Language teachers follow the roller-coaster model to ensure that a balance of English and Spanish instruction is in place.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In the Dual Language program, core content instruction takes place in both Spanish and English. observations.programme_model_source_text: The self-contained One-Way Dual Language Bilingual Education model is implemented in grades K-5 in our school. We follow a 50/50 roller coaster model, alternating between English and Spanish every other day. All subjects follow this model except for Writing, with each unit alternating between English and Spanish (i.e., The entire unit is taught in one language). English proficient students and ELLs are integrated 100% of the instructional day. On alternating days, the instructional language of the day is English to support our ELLs and meet their mandated English services. On the following day, the instructional language will be Spanish to support Home Language Arts and meet the goals of our Dual Language Bilingual Education program. The instructional language for each day is posted outside and inside the classroom so that the students are aware if it is an English day or a Spanish day of learning. Our English proficient students share the same heritage language (Spanish) and are learning English and Spanish as their target languages. Students will be able to have rich experiences in both languages and they will be supported according to their needs. Scaffolding and differentiated instruction are provided depending on the students' learning needs and their different learning styles.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Social Studies, Science, Math, and Language Arts are taught in both English and Spanish. The DLBE model is a 50/50 language model. DBN: 32K086 School: P.S. 086 The Irvington 139 of 199

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our Dual language program aims to offer our students the opportunity to become bilingual, biliterate, and bicultural while improving student academic ability in two languages ( English and Spanish ). Currently, we have a 2-way Dual-Language model. Instruction is designed to include both languages through a 50:50 language allocation model (50% of instructional time is conducted in English and 50% is conducted in Spanish). The goal is to provide a balanced and equitable learning experience in both languages. The language of instruction is delivered on alternating days. In the Two-Way Dual Language program, emergent literacy is taught in a sequential manner. Students receive strong literacy development instruction in their native language (Spanish) as well as in their second language (English). Teachers ensure that systematic and explicit instruction is provided in both languages to support students' language acquisition and literacy skills. They create a language-rich environment that offers ample opportunities for students to practice and engage with both languages. Additionally, teachers highlight cognates (words that are similar in both languages) and help students make connections between English and Spanish, facilitating their language development and cross-linguistic understanding.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In the Two-Way Dual Language program at P.S. 106, each core content area is taught in both English and the target language, which is Spanish. This language allocation remains consistent from Kindergarten to 5th grade. DBN: 32K106 School: P.S. 106 Edward Everett Hale 145 of 206

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our DLBE program is a self-contained, developmental, language-enriched, bilingual education program that integrates students who are native English language speakers with native speakers of Spanish 100% of the day. Students receive half the instruction in English and half in the target language Spanish. Language is taught through content areas as well as literacy. In Grades K-5 we use the roller-coaster model, where half of the day’s lessons are in English and half in Spanish for the entire week. The next week, the schedule is inverted. If the week before English was taught in the morning and Spanish in the afternoon, then Spanish would be taught in the morning with English in the afternoon. The roller - coaster method was put in place to accommodate the ML/ELLs mandated weekly minutes. When morning instruction begins in English, English proficient students and ELLs are integrated 50 percent of the instructional day. When morning instruction begins in Spanish, English proficient students and ELLs are integrated 50 percent of the the instructional day. The goal is to develop bilingual and biliterate academic goals in both English and Spanish for all students.

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our Dual Language classrooms are predicated on the following ideas and principle of educating students in a self- contained 50/50 Dual Language Model Classroom: --Students in dual language programs do as well or better than students learning only in English on standardized tests given in English. --Students participating in dual language programs close the achievement gap that currently exists between English Language Learners and general education students. --Students in dual language programs develop respect for multiple cultural heritages. -- Students' cognitive function is positively impacted when they learn a second language. --Students in dual language programs increase their marketable skills in a global society. In Kindergarten to fifth Grade, at PS 299, dual language follows a self contained 50/50 model. This simply means that our students will learn Spanish and English from the same teacher in the same classroom, on alternating days. The classrooms reflect both languages equally. Instruction will be delivered in the target language of the day. Our dual language classrooms have a one-way DLBE model, in which mostly/all of the students are ELLs. All students' needs are met and the use of their native language on alternate days assures that we not only affirm biculturalism, but also support all students equally. Dual language allows all students to transfer academic skills in the native language to a new language on any given day. Sample Week 1: Monday Spanish Tuesday English Wednesday Spanish Thursday English Friday Spanish Sample Week 2: Monday English Tuesday Spanish Wednesday English Thursday Spanish Friday English.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Spanish and English are utilized for all subject areas except for native language development and ELA, specifically for: mathematics, social studies and science. DBN: 32K299 School: P.S. 299 Thomas Warren Field 147 of 204

All students' needs are met and the use of their native language on alternate days assures that we not only affirm biculturalism, but also support all students equally. Dual language allows all students to transfer academic skills in the native language to a new language on any given day. Sample Week 1: Monday Spanish Tuesday English Wednesday Spanish Thursday English Friday Spanish Sample Week 2: Monday English Tuesday Spanish Wednesday English Thursday Spanish Friday English.   Spanish and English are utilized for all subject areas except for native language development and ELA, specifically for: mathematics, social studies and science. observations.programme_model_source_text: In both programs offered at PS 112 (Stand Alone ENL and Dual Language), teachers plan intentionally for content, literacy, and language objectives using a variety of curricula, resources, and data. All curricula is aligned to the NYS Next Generation Standards, NYCDOE Science Scope and Sequence and Next Generation Learning Science Standards, NYCDOE Social Studies Scope and Sequence, and NYS New Language Arts Progressions (NLAP) and Home Language Arts Progressions (HLAP). Literacy Content/ Curriculum: In Dual Language Classrooms, we teach literacy instruction for 120 minutes in the language of the day. Phonics: We teach phonics instruction in the child's language of dominance in kindergarten (small groups) as well as guided reading- sequential literacy. For English Instruction we use Fundations, and for Spanish Instruction we use Estrellita. Word Study Phonics: In grades 1-2 we deliver simultaneous literacy with the exception of students who need intervention in their language of dominance (alternate days/ roller coaster model 50/50), and therefore receive explicit phonics instruction in their language of dominance, as determined by battery of assessments in both languages. For English Instruction we use Fundations, and for Spanish Instruction we use Palabras a su Paso Word Study (HLA) and Estrellita Word Study for intervention. Language objectives are planned for all multilingual learners. Reading: In all grades we deliver explicit reading instruction using the comprehensive framework , balanced literacy model, through simultaneous literacy in both languages (alternate days/ roller coaster model 50/50). We teach reading lessons through the Teachers College Reading Writing Project (TCRWP). We also plan for shared reading lessons using various resources. For Spanish, we also purchased Adelante Program to support with shared reading lessons and guided reading lessons. We plan intentionally for English lessons using scaffolds and supports. Guided Reading/ Small group reading: In kindergarten, and for intervention throughout the grades, we use language of dominance to support reading development. We use Leveled Literacy Intervention (LLI) , Fountas and Pinell Guided Reading program, Reach, English Language Learner Texts Sets/ Sun Dance (all English) and Adelante (Spanish), as well as other resources. Writing : In all grades we deliver explicit writing instruction using the comprehensive framework , balanced literacy model, through simultaneous literacy. We teach writing lessons through the Teachers College Reading Writing Project (TCRWP). We also plan for shared writing and interactive writing lessons using various resources. We plan intentionally for English lessons using scaffolds and supports. Writing Units of studies are conducted in alternating languages (Spanish/ English -4 Units in Spanish and 4 Units in English). Scaffolds provided aligned with the work from "Scaffolding Language, Scaffolding Learning" (Pauline Gibbons) and "Differentiating for English Language Learners" (Fairbairn and Jones) Literacy through Content Area: Based on the work from Lesaux and Harris, Cultivating knowledge Building Language, teachers designed inter-disciplinary lessons using the four hallmarks for Advanced Literacy. Teachers explicitly plan for all four modalities within content area- social studies or science (Using Next Generation Learning Standards, NYCDOE Scope and Sequence, and Next Generation Learning Science Standards). In ENL standalone and Integrated Programs: , For students in these classrooms we teach literacy instruction for 120 minutes in English, with ENL teacher providing explicit scaffolds and supports as per the school-wide literacy programs. DBN: 04M112 School: P.S. 112 Jose Celso Barbosa 152 of 213 Phonics: ENL teacher supplements using Words their Way for Stand Alone ENL. Reading: ENL teacher supplements using Reach into Phonics, English Language Learners Text Sets, online resources such as NatGeo Panorama, and other resources which support ENL development. Math Curriculum: Investigation and Context for Learning with scaffolds provided to support ENL progression and HL Support (Spanish). In Dual Language Programs we abide to the alternate day, roller coaster 50/50 model. Science and Social Studies: Inquiry-based units which integrate literacy and the NYCDOE Scope and Sequence for Science, Next Generation Learning Science Standards, Amplify Science Program (just purchased 2019), NYCDOE Scope and Sequence for Social Studies are used. -Integration of academic collaborative conversations using the work from Stanford University, "Constructive Classroom Conversations: -Mastering the Language of the Common Core State Standards in all classrooms. We meet in dual language vertical teams inclusive of ENL coordinator, study groups, and professional learning communities to create lessons which support the diverse linguistic needs for our students. As such, we continue to engage in best practices in order to plan intentionally for highly-effective lessons, deliver them, and share results as exemplars to our colleagues. Analyze Conversation Analysis Tool from Stanford NovaEd online course, to assess student to student conversations. We use Universal English Language Development Speaking Rubrics to assess for oral language development. Teacher teams meet and analyze student transcripts and videos using these rubrics along with the above data and resources to intentionally target language outcomes. Teacher teams also analyze the complexity of texts using the resources from Nonie Lesaux and Aida Walqui to analyze and plan for the language demands. The following instructional strategies are used: (from but not limited to): Study group: from Ruth Sweeney’s text: Connecting Content and Academic Language for ELLs and Struggling Students, and Gibbons text: Scaffolding Language, Scaffolding Learning, teachers plan intentionally for comprehensible, language), "Differentiating for English Language Learners" (Fairbairn and Jones), and Cultivating knowledge Building Language, teachers designed inter-disciplinary lessons using the four hallmarks for Advanced Literacy (Lesaux and Harris). To support background knowledge and vocabulary, we use an inquiry-based approach to learning (thematic / interdisciplinary), where students are immersed in hands-on experiences through virutal field trips, media, visual aids, and frontloading of vocabulary. We also use graphic organizers such as concept maps and semantic maps to support the oral language development and academic language. Technology is woven into the curriculum as a means to differentiate and support all learners in all four modalities. DBN: 04M112 School: P.S. 112 Jose Celso Barbosa 153 of 213 Sentence frames and sentence starters (differentiated for various proficiency levels) are provided to support students engaging in academic discourse. Explicit teaching of Tier 2 words throughout the school allows for the development of academic vocabulary for all students. We also address syntax and vocabulary intentionally within our shared reading texts (which are aligned to standard 10 and are representative of various content areas/informational texts) which allow for students to dissect and interpret a familiar text for multiple opportunities.

observations.programme_model_source_text: The DL program is a 50/50 two-way program. For 3rd through 5th grade, the school uses a side-by-side model in which students alternate their language of instruction each day so that students receive instruction in core subjects in both English and Spanish. The 6th grade DL class is self-contained and receives instruction in core subjects in both English and Spanish within one day. The 7th and 8th grade DL classes receive instruction in core subjects in both English and Spanish within one day. DL classes are homogeneous in grade, and the classes are taught by one teacher team throughout the day or travel as one group to different teacher teams by content. DL classes are heterogeneous in terms of proficiency level, so English proficient students and ELLs are integrated for 100% of the instructional day. ELLs in the DL program performing at the Entering, Emerging, or Transitioning proficiency levels receive standalone instruction per CR Part 154.2. The groups of students for standalone instruction may be heterogeneous in grade (spanning no more than two grade bands) and proficiency level (spanning between Entering to Transitioning). Stand-alone ENL instruction is provided by a certified ENL instructor 180 minutes across the week, in order to help students acquire the English Language needed to access the work in the core subject areas. Differentiated direct instruction in reading, writing, listening and speaking is provided based on the literacy levels of the children. Instruction is provided by way of mini-lessons to the whole class, small group instruction and independent work.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In the 3rd and 4th grade DL program, Math is taught in both Spanish and English. Reading and Writing are taught in Spanish and English. Science is taught only in English and Social Studies is taught only in Spanish. In the 5th grade DL program, Math is taught in both Spanish and English. Reading and Writing are taught in Spanish and English. Science is taught in Spanish only and Social Studies is taught in English. In the 6th grade DL program, Math is taught in both Spanish and English. Reading and Writing are taught in Spanish and English. Science is taught in Spanish and Social Studies is taught in English. In the 7th grade DL program, Science and Social Studies are taught in Spanish, and ELA and math are taught in English. In the 8th grade DL program, Science and Social Studies are taught in Spanish, and ELA and Math are taught in English. DBN: 04M206 School: P.S. 206 Jose Celso Barbosa 178 of 226

observations.programme_model_source_text: This school year our school is implementing a Pre-Kindergarten to fifth grade self-contained Dual Language Program. Our Dual Language Program is conducted in English (50%) and in Spanish (50%), one day in each language. The class is composed of 50% ELLs and 50% non ELLS (EPs). All content area subjects are taught bilingually in English and Spanish. The goal is to develop skills in reading, listening, writing, and speaking in the two languages. One licensed teacher will instruct the children in their first language and second language, one day in English and the other in Spanish. Both languages are not taught simultaneously. The primary language acquisition goals of dual language programs are the development of grade-level-appropriate bilingual and biliterate academic skills in both English and the target language for all students. Students are also instructed and encouraged to read grade level books in both languages, providing them books in both languages from the classroom library.

observations.programme_model_source_text: At 06M311 the Dual Language Program follows a one-way (self-contained) model where ELLs and non-ELLs learn two languages in one classroom with one teacher who switches the language of instruction. Our Dual Language Program is simultaneous with a 50% English and 50% Target Language/Spanish. Our language allocation policy varies by grade: In K-1, we follow an alternating day model. For example, students’ instructional language is Spanish on Monday, Wednesday and Friday and in English on Tuesday and Thursday. In grade 2 , we follow an alternating half-day model for alternating 1-week cycles so that students are equally exposed to all content areas in both languages. In the half-day model, students receive instruction in one language in the morning and another language in the afternoon. In grade 3-4 , we follow an alternating half-day model for a 3-2-3 week cycle (example: 3 English- 2 Spanish- 3 English) so that students are equally exposed to all content areas in both languages. In the half-day model, students receive instruction in one language in the morning and another language in the afternoon. In grades 5th - 8th, we follow a full day language distribution for a 3-2-3 week cycle (example: 3 English- 2 Spanish- 3 English). The Literacy Intervention program is a pullout program that schedules students in small groups (homogeneous) or in one-to-one rations. Scheduling of students varies from two periods per week to four periods per week, as needed.
observations.subject_language_source_text: As a 50-50 Dual Language Model our students are immersed in both English and Spanish in all content areas (ELA/HLA, Math, Science & Social Studies) DBN: 06M311 School: Amistad Dual Language School 138 of 192

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our Dual-Language Program in our school consists of self-contained classes that use the roller coaster model. Instruction is delivered 50% of the time in English and 50% in Spanish. In this model, approximately half of the students are English proficient and the other half is Spanish dominant. The classrooms are heterogeneous in proficiency levels in both English and Spanish. All teachers work collaboratively with the classroom teacher to support ENL students. Our English-proficient students and emergent bilingual learners (EBLs) are integrated for 100% of the instructional day except when our EBLs receive their ENL services.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In our Dual-Language Program roller coaster model, students receive all content areas in both English and Spanish. Some of the instructional approaches and methodologies used to make content comprehensible and to enrich language development are visual support, cooperative learning groups, vocabulary building support, thematic approaches, The Language Experience Approach, project-based learning, and differentiated instruction. These approaches and methodologies are incorporated on a daily basis to meet the needs of English Language learners based on their language and academic needs. observations.programme_model_source_text: In Kindergarten, all classes follow a self-contained 60/40 language model, with 60% of instruction in Spanish and 40% in English. Content areas are taught in Spanish on Mondays and Wednesdays, and in English on Tuesdays and Thursdays, providing a strong foundation in both languages. In 1st grade, all classes follow a self-contained 50/50 language model, with 50% of instruction in Spanish and 50% in English. Content areas are taught in Spanish on Mondays and Wednesdays, and in English on Tuesdays and Thursdays and half a day on Friday, providing a strong foundation in both languages. From 2nd through 5th grade, all ICT (Integrated Co-Teaching) classes implement a 50/50 Dual Language model, with instruction alternating between Spanish and English across content areas. Specifically, instruction is delivered in Spanish on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Friday mornings, and in English on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Friday afternoons. Beginning in 2nd grade and continuing through 4th grade, students in General Education classes follow a side-by-side model, where all content is delivered by two teachers—one teaching exclusively in Spanish and the other in English— in separate classrooms. Students alternate between the two classrooms on a daily basis, ensuring balanced exposure to both languages. English-proficient and ELL students are integrated throughout the school day based on their individual language needs and the subject area. The only exception is during stand-alone ENL instruction, which is provided separately for students at the Entering and Emerging levels, as required by state regulations.

observations.programme_model_source_text: P.S. 4 implements a One-Way Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) model with one class per grade, Kindergarten through 5th grade. This model uses a 50/50 simultaneous language distribution, where students receive half of their instruction in English and half in Spanish. Classroom teachers teach all core content areas—Literacy, Math, Science, and Social Studies—in both languages. Literacy follows the Expeditionary Learning (EL) curriculum, alternating language by unit within each module (e.g., Unit 1 in English, Unit 2 in Spanish, Unit 3 in English) to maintain the 50/50 balance. observations.programme_model_source_text: The Dual Language model implemented is a Spanish One-Way Immersion, self-contained, 50/50 model. English proficient students and ELLs are integrated for 100% of the instructional day. Literacy instruction will alternate units of study in English (ELA) and Spanish (HLA). Math units will also alternate between English and Spanish. When the literacy unit is being taught in English, the math unit will be taught in Spanish, and vice versa. For newcomer ELLs, Illustrative Math and Expeditionary Learning Literacy will always be available as a native language support. For grades K-2, emergent literacy skills in both languages will be taught every day, using Fundations, Heggerty, Imagine Español, and Aprendo Leyendo. For the entirety of the school year, Science will be taught in English using Amplify Science, while Social Studies will be taught in Spanish using Passport to Social Studies and other instructional resources. Linguistic summaries of the lessons will be provided in each lesson to support the development in both languages of the lessons will be provided in each lesson to support the development in both languages.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Literacy and Math content will be taught equally in Spanish and English using an alternating unit schedule. Science will be taught in English and Social Studies will be taught in Spanish. DBN: 06M008 School: P.S. 008 Luis Belliard 149 of 216

Our philosophy is predicated on children being able to learn from each other and to promote each other's academic growth.

observations.programme_model_source_text: The Dual Language model that is used in the school is self-contained, 50/50 model, alternating English and Spanish every other day with Literacy mostly instructed in English with Spanish used as a support. All CORE subjects( literacy, math, science, and social studies) alternate every other day. For grades K-2, emergent literacy skills in both languages will be taught, using Fundations, Heggerty, and Estrellita. This model allows for ELL students and proficient English students to participate in a class together in English and Spanish. For the ELL students, in particular, it is beneficial because while they are learning the second language in school, they still can develop their native language skills. For students who were never ELLs the exposure to a second language from their school community, teacher, classmates, and curriculum resources in Spanish promote biliteracy. For new arrivals in the program or students who are new to DL there are many targeted small groups, where either English or Spanish is used for support. The use of technology has really allowed students to engage in the new language when they are learning at home and at school to improve linguistic competency. The language allocation adopted is 50% English and 50% Spanish.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Literacy(EL) is taught mostly in English with other literacy materials in Spanish (Heggerty, IL, Science and Social Studies) to support students and/or to layer the text. Math, Science, Social Studies is instructed in both languages, alternating days. DBN: 06M153 School: P.S. 153 Adam Clayton Powell 150 of 224

observations.programme_model_source_text: a. Dual Language Bilingual Education Model and Student Integration At PS 178M, we implement a self-contained Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) model designed to foster biliteracy and academic excellence for all students. In this model, English Proficient (EP) students and English Language Learners (ELLs) are fully integrated within the same classroom throughout the entire instructional day across all grade levels. This intentional integration creates a rich linguistic environment where students serve as authentic language models for one another, fostering reciprocal language development in both Spanish and English. The percentage of instructional time dedicated to each language varies by grade level, ensuring a developmentally appropriate and effective pathway to biliteracy: Kindergarten (80% Spanish / 20% English): In Kindergarten, we initiate with an 80/20 language allocation model. This approach prioritizes a strong foundation in Spanish literacy and content learning, providing English Proficient students with immersive exposure to Spanish while giving our entering ELLs a solid boost in their heritage language proficiency. This early emphasis supports sustained Spanish language growth into the higher grades. Grades 1-4 (50% Spanish / 50% English): From first through fourth grade, our program transitions to a balanced 50/50 language allocation. Language separation within this model is achieved primarily through alternating days of instruction in each language or through alternating units of study, ensuring equal exposure and deep learning in both Spanish and English across the entire curriculum, including the literacy block and content areas. Fifth Grade (Compartmentalized Subject Instruction with Dual Language): By fifth grade, students receive compartmentalized instruction by subject. While core content subjects are predominantly taught in English, students continue to receive dedicated Dual Language instruction 2-3 times per week, flexibly scheduled, to maintain and advance their Spanish language proficiency. Curriculum Integration and Targeted Support: Our curriculum for both languages is meticulously planned and mapped by teachers who meet regularly to ensure comprehensive coverage without overlap or gaps. Emergent literacy skills are developed simultaneously in both languages within the context of our grade-level language allocation models. For students who demonstrate a need based on careful ongoing assessment and monitoring (e.g., those entering with minimal pre-literacy skills or performing below grade level), we provide targeted, differentiated instruction. This may include temporary, intensive guided reading intervention in their dominant language to accelerate their reading performance. Our experience shows this direct support in their native language significantly improves overall literacy outcomes in both their heritage language and English. Once adequate progress is achieved, students seamlessly transition back into the full 50/50 time model.
observations.subject_language_source_text: b. Language of Instruction for Core Content Areas The language of instruction for core content areas at PS 178M is determined by the specific Dual Language program model implemented at each grade level, ensuring a balanced and comprehensive approach to biliteracy: Kindergarten (80% Spanish / 20% English Model): DBN: 06M178 School: Professor Juan Bosch Public School 144 of 195 The majority of Mathematics, Science, and Social Studies content instruction is delivered in Spanish. English is introduced through dedicated English instructional blocks and integrated into content as appropriate for the 20% English allocation. Home Language Arts (HLA) instruction focuses on Spanish literacy, while initial English Language Arts (ELA) foundations are laid through integrated ENL. Grades 1-4 (50% Spanish / 50% English Alternate-Day Model): Core content areas, including Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, English Language Arts (ELA), and Home Language Arts (HLA), are taught in both languages. Instruction occurs on alternating days, meaning that on Spanish days, all core content is delivered in Spanish, and on English days, all core content is delivered in English. This ensures equal exposure and development of academic vocabulary and concepts in both languages across the curriculum. Fifth Grade (Compartmentalized Subject Instruction): In fifth grade, English Language Arts (ELA) is taught in English. Core content areas such as Mathematics and Science are also primarily taught in English. However, students continue to receive dedicated Dual Language instruction 2-3 times per week, flexibly scheduled. During this block, students focus on Spanish literacy (grammar, reading, and writing), ensuring the continued development of advanced academic language in Spanish. We are also very project-driven, and a lot of these projects and special activities will involve Social Studies, Geography, and research projects, allowing for integrated content learning within the Spanish Dual Language block. DBN: 06M178 School: Professor Juan Bosch Public School 145 of 195

This approach prioritizes a strong foundation in Spanish literacy and content learning, providing English Proficient students with immersive exposure to Spanish while giving our entering ELLs a solid boost in their heritage language proficiency. This early emphasis supports sustained Spanish language growth into the higher grades. Grades 1-4 (50% Spanish / 50% English): From first through fourth grade, our program transitions to a balanced 50/50 language allocation. Language separation within this model is achieved primarily through alternating days of instruction in each language or through alternating units of study, ensuring equal exposure and deep learning in both Spanish and English across the entire curriculum, including the literacy block and content areas. Fifth Grade (Compartmentalized Subject Instruction with Dual Language): By fifth grade, students receive compartmentalized instruction by subject. While core content subjects are predominantly taught in English, students continue to receive dedicated Dual Language instruction 2-3 times per week, flexibly scheduled, to maintain and advance their Spanish language proficiency. Curriculum Integration and Targeted Support: Our curriculum for both languages is meticulously planned and mapped by teachers who meet regularly to ensure comprehensive coverage without overlap or gaps. Emergent literacy skills are developed simultaneously in both languages within the context of our grade-level language allocation models. For students who demonstrate a need based on careful ongoing assessment and monitoring (e.g., those entering with minimal pre-literacy skills or performing below grade level), we provide targeted, differentiated instruction. This may include temporary, intensive guided reading intervention in their dominant language to accelerate their reading performance. Our experience shows this direct support in their native language significantly improves overall literacy outcomes in both their heritage language and English. Once adequate progress is achieved, students seamlessly transition back into the full 50/50 time model.   b. Language of Instruction for Core Content Areas The language of instruction for core content areas at PS 178M is determined by the specific Dual Language program model implemented at each grade level, ensuring a balanced and comprehensive approach to biliteracy: Kindergarten (80% Spanish / 20% English Model): DBN: 06M178 School: Professor Juan Bosch Public School 144 of 195 The majority of Mathematics, Science, and Social Studies content instruction is delivered in Spanish. English is introduced through dedicated English instructional blocks and integrated into content as appropriate for the 20% English allocation. Home Language Arts (HLA) instruction focuses on Spanish literacy, while initial English Language Arts (ELA) foundations are laid through integrated ENL. Grades 1-4 (50% Spanish / 50% English Alternate-Day Model): Core content areas, including Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, English Language Arts (ELA), and Home Language Arts (HLA), are taught in both languages. Instruction occurs on alternating days, meaning that on Spanish days, all core content is delivered in Spanish, and on English days, all core content is delivered in English. This ensures equal exposure and development of academic vocabulary and concepts in both languages across the curriculum. Fifth Grade (Compartmentalized Subject Instruction): In fifth grade, English Language Arts (ELA) is taught in English. Core content areas such as Mathematics and Science are also primarily taught in English. However, students continue to receive dedicated Dual Language instruction 2-3 times per week, flexibly scheduled. During this block, students focus on Spanish literacy (grammar, reading, and writing), ensuring the continued development of advanced academic language in Spanish. We are also very project-driven, and a lot of these projects and special activities will involve Social Studies, Geography, and research projects, allowing for integrated content learning within the Spanish Dual Language block. observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school implements a 50/50 Dual Language Bilingual Education (DLBE) Spanish model across grades Pre-K through 5, designed to promote language equity and biliteracy for both English proficient students and English Language Learners (ELLs). In grades Pre-K to 2, the program follows a roller coaster model, where instruction alternates by weeks between Spanish and English. This means that students may begin a week with Spanish instruction and end with English, or vice versa, rotating the subjects covered in the partner language. This approach maintains a balanced 50/50 distribution of language instruction while providing varied exposure and reinforcement of both languages throughout the week. In the upper elementary grades (3–5), the DLBE Spanish model continues with a roller coaster structure based on literacy units. Literacy instruction cycles between languages across units to ensure that students build background knowledge, apply skills, and produce final projects in both English and Spanish over the academic year. When literacy instruction is conducted in English (ie: reading, writing, and additional language and literacy blocks) core content areas like math and science are taught in Spanish. Conversely, when literacy units switch to Spanish, math and science instruction shift to English, creating integrated and complementary bilingual learning experiences aligned with the literacy overview without interfering with each other. Throughout all grade levels, both English proficient students and ELLs are fully integrated within the same classrooms, promoting inclusive learning environments in both General Education and Integrated Co-Teaching settings.
observations.subject_language_source_text: In elementary grades (K through 5), all core and content areas are delivered in both English and Spanish following the weekly or unit-based roller coaster model. This means that students experience instruction in all subjects in Spanish during one week or unit and in English during the next, ensuring balanced bilingual exposure across the academic year. In middle school and high school (grades 6–12), all core and content area instruction is delivered in English, with targeted ENL supports integrated across subjects to meet the language development needs of English Language Learners. This model ensures access to grade-level content while providing necessary scaffolds to support academic success. DBN: 06M348 School: Washington Heights Expeditionary Learning School 137 of 201

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our Dual Language program follows a self-contained model in which the teacher provides instruction in both English and Spanish. Students receive instruction in all content areas in both languages. ENL instructional minutes are embedded into lessons across all content areas, including ELA, to support entry points and provide access for students at various proficiency levels. These strategies ensure that English Language Learners (ELLs) engage meaningfully with the curriculum, regardless of the subject area. The Dual Language program begins in Pre-K, Kindergarten, 1st grade, 2nd grade, and 3rd grade with plans to extend the program over at least five years. The program follows a 90/10 model in Kindergarten, 80/20 in 1st grade, a 70/30 model in 2nd grade and a 50/50 model in 3rd grade. Our Dual Language program aims for: Bilingualism (the ability to speak fluently in two languages), Biliteracy (the ability to read and write in two languages), Academic achievement equal to or greater than that of students in non-dual language programs, and Cross-cultural competence. Teachers maintain the separation of languages for instruction, ensuring that skills taught in each language are coordinated to maximize cross-linguistic transfer and support learning in content areas. Flexible grouping and differentiation are used to meet the needs of both native speakers and language learners. Literacy development in both languages proceeds at a sufficient pace, ensuring that students' language skills are strong enough to meet the increased academic demands of the upper grades.
observations.subject_language_source_text: For the DL classes, all content areas are taught in Spanish at the appropriate model for the grade with a daily period of Phonics in English to develop English Language Skills. Students in our DL programs also exposed to additional English Instruction through our Music, Dance, Art, Technology and Physical Education. DBN: 07X025 School: P.S. 025 Bilingual School 149 of 195

Teachers maintain the separation of languages for instruction, ensuring that skills taught in each language are coordinated to maximize cross-linguistic transfer and support learning in content areas. Flexible grouping and differentiation are used to meet the needs of both native speakers and language learners. Literacy development in both languages proceeds at a sufficient pace, ensuring that students' language skills are strong enough to meet the increased academic demands of the upper grades.   For the DL classes, all content areas are taught in Spanish at the appropriate model for the grade with a daily period of Phonics in English to develop English Language Skills. Students in our DL programs also exposed to additional English Instruction through our Music, Dance, Art, Technology and Physical Education. DBN: 07X025 School: P.S. 025 Bilingual School 149 of 195

observations.programme_model_source_text: We utilize a two-way, side-by-side Dual Language (DL) model that integrates English proficient students, former English Language Learners (ELLs), and current ELLs together in the same classroom for 100% of the instructional day. Our DL teachers are departmentalized by content area and work in grade-level pairs. Each teacher is responsible for two consecutive grade levels (e.g., K–1, 2–3, or 4–5) and specializes in two core content areas—either English Language Arts (ELA) & Social Studies or Math & Science. For example, in the Kindergarten–1st grade DL team: One teacher teaches Math and Science to both Kindergarten and 1st grade students. The partner teacher teaches ELA and Social Studies to the same students. This structure is mirrored in the 2nd–3rd and 4th–5th grade DL classrooms, ensuring consistency, specialization, and deep content expertise within a collaborative teaching environment.
observations.subject_language_source_text: The core content is delivered in both English and Spanish, alternating by day. On one day, all subjects are taught in English; on the next, all subjects are taught in Spanish. DBN: 07X049 School: P.S. 049 Willis Avenue 152 of 204

observations.programme_model_source_text: P.S. 48 implemented a Dual Language program in the Kindergarten level in Fall 2017 and monitors the implications it might have on student progress across the content areas. This was the beginning of a roll out over the next 6 years in order to create a DL program on each grade level with one class per grade being dual language. PS 48 plans, reflects, and builds best practices and school personnel capacity for implementing a successful DL program. The school will utilize the DMLLS' "Checklist of Model Dual Language Enrichment Programs" to guide the process. Our school will determine ELL eligibility through the NYSITELL (and thus the Spanish home language students for the program). For English home language students, school staff will be trained to interview proficiency in English. This program is offered in both in person and remote options (should the need arise) to ensure seamless preparation for external events that may alter the educational experience at our school. The DL program is two way dual language program that is self-contained where half the students have a home language of Spanish who will deepen their Spanish literacy skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing, and visual literacy) while learning English in an academic setting. Concurrently, the other half of the students have an English home language, and will build on their English skills to develop Spanish-English bilteracy. The program is a commitment on the behalf of PS 48 for the school community. Families commit to ensuring that their child maintains participation in the program in subsequent years to build and deepen literacy skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing, and visual literacy) in both languages. One classroom teacher is responsible for instruction in both languages. This program is offered in both in person and remote options (should the need arise).
observations.subject_language_source_text: Core content is taught in both Spanish and English, including literacy (HMH), mathematics, social studies, and science curriculum. Curriculum is aligned to CCLS/NGLS and NYCDOE pacing charts, utilizes HMH Into Reading literacy (reading and writing), 10-10-10, Adelante, Math Problem of the Day, and Amplify Math materials, that are augments by supplemental materials, including dual language texts that support phonics, comprehension, vocabulary, and content development in both languages.
