For English home language students, school staff will be trained to interview proficiency in English. This program is offered in both in person and remote options (should the need arise) to ensure seamless preparation for external events that may alter the educational experience at our school. The DL program is two way dual language program that is self-contained where half the students have a home language of Spanish who will deepen their Spanish literacy skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing, and visual literacy) while learning English in an academic setting. Concurrently, the other half of the students have an English home language, and will build on their English skills to develop Spanish-English bilteracy. The program is a commitment on the behalf of PS 48 for the school community. Families commit to ensuring that their child maintains participation in the program in subsequent years to build and deepen literacy skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing, and visual literacy) in both languages. One classroom teacher is responsible for instruction in both languages. This program is offered in both in person and remote options (should the need arise).   Core content is taught in both Spanish and English, including literacy (HMH), mathematics, social studies, and science curriculum. Curriculum is aligned to CCLS/NGLS and NYCDOE pacing charts, utilizes HMH Into Reading literacy (reading and writing), 10-10-10, Adelante, Math Problem of the Day, and Amplify Math materials, that are augments by supplemental materials, including dual language texts that support phonics, comprehension, vocabulary, and content development in both languages. observations.programme_model_source_text: The Two-Way Immersion (TWI) program—commonly known as a Dual Language (DL) education program—aims to develop full oral, reading, and writing proficiency in two languages for all students. This model includes both English Language Learners (ELLs) and English-proficient students, who learn academic content in both English and the partner language (Spanish) during designated times. At PS 53X, the Dual Language program is implemented in self-contained classrooms, beginning in Kindergarten. The current Kindergarten class includes both Spanish-speaking newcomers and English-speaking students, creating an authentic language-rich environment that supports bilingualism and biliteracy development for all learners. Key features of the DL program at PS 53X include: Instruction that follows a “language of the week” model, alternating weekly between English and Spanish All core subjects (ELA, Math, Science, Social Studies) taught in both languages throughout the school year Emphasis on building students’ academic content knowledge while developing bilingual, biliterate, and multicultural competencies This program is designed to foster equity and inclusion, providing students from diverse language backgrounds with the tools to succeed academically while developing fluency in two languages. Please refer to the sample schedule below for a detailed look at how instruction is organized across the week.

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our Dual Language program uses the one way model. One bilingual teacher teaches in English and Spanish. English proficient students and ELLs are integrated 100% of the instructional day. Content subjects are taught in English and Spanish alternating days utilizing 50 / 50. For example, if ELA is taught in Spanish for one day, Math is taught in English that same day. Then the following day ELA is taught in English and Math in Spanish. Appropriate differentiation and scaffolds are provided for students in the respective languages. The one way model uses HMH: Into Reading / Arriba la Lectura and Eureka Math in both English and Spanish for all grades. K - 3 uses Heggerty (English) and Estrellita (Spanish) for phonemic awareness in both languages. Aprendo Leyendo (Spanish) has been incorporated as well in small group instruction.
observations.subject_language_source_text: All core content areas are taught in both English and Spanish, alternating on a daily basis. DBN: 09X109 School: P.S. 109 Sedgwick 155 of 219

observations.programme_model_source_text: In the side-by-side model (K-2) students alternate between two classrooms every other day, one teacher delivers instruction in English and the other in Spanish (NLA). The lessons are continued the next day in the target language. The teacher who possesses a bilingual extension will deliver the instruction in English and/or in Spanish depending on the programming. HLA is provided on the Spanish days by the Spanish teacher throughout the entire day. Stand alone ENL minutes is provided by a n ESOL teacher for emerging/entering level and integrated ENL/ELA is provided by the bilingual certified teacher or co-taught by a n ESOL teacher and common branch certified teacher . The ENL teacher works collaboratively with the classroom teacher to plan accordingly, meet student needs and provide the minutes according to their proficiency levels. In the side-by-side model in grades K-2, teachers hold a common branch license with a bilingual extension. These teachers deliver integrated ENL/ELA for all students. Emerging and entering students receive their additional 90 or 180 minutes in a pull-out stand-alone ENL setting with a n ESOL teacher. One of the teachers in the side-by-side model is the Spanish teacher who delivers HLA instructional minutes. As the classes switch from Spanish to English every other day, this ensures students receive all HLA, ELA and ENL instructional minutes. In the departmentalized model in grades 3-5, the teacher hold a common branch license with a bilingual extension. This teacher delivers all ENL, ELA and HLA minutes. HLA instructional minutes are delivered through social studies, science and math. Emerging and entering students also receive their standalone ENL minutes (90 or 180) with a n ESOL teacher. 6th-8th grade students receive standalone ENL minutes by an ESOL teacher and integrated ENL/ELA by a n ESOL teacher and a n ELA certified teacher. The program model and minutes are determined by the level of proficiency. HLA for 6th- 8th grade is delivered through the content area in social studies, science and math by a content area teacher with a bilingual extension.
observations.subject_language_source_text: Core content areas are taught in both English and Spanish. DBN: 09X218 School: P.S./I.S. 218 Rafael Hernandez Dual Language Magnet School 155 of 200

observations.programme_model_source_text: Our school implements the Two-Way Immersion (TWI) Dual Language Bilingual Education model in a self-contained setting. Specifically, we use a 50:50 model, where instruction is delivered equally in English and the partner language (Spanish). Our school's Two-Way Immersion (TWI) Dual Language Bilingual Education model, using a 50:50 language allocation, fully integrates English proficient students and ELLs throughout the instructional day. By alternating the language of instruction on a daily basis within a two-week cycle, we ensure that all students receive equal exposure to both English and Spanish, promoting bilingualism, biliteracy, and academic success for all students.
observations.subject_language_source_text: On days designated for English instruction, Language Arts is taught entirely in English. This includes reading, writing, listening, and speaking activities. On days designated for Spanish instruction, Language Arts is taught entirely in Spanish, focusing on developing literacy skills in the target language. Mathematics instruction alternates between English and Spanish according to the daily schedule. For example, if Monday is an English day, math is taught in English, and if Tuesday is a Spanish day, math is taught in Spanish. This ensures that students develop the ability to understand and apply mathematical concepts in both languages. For Science and Social Studies instruction will take place in English as we have no Bilingual certified cluster teachers for Science or Social Studies. However, Science and Social Studies is very much embedded within out ELA (HMH) curriculum. So if it is a Spanish day and the topic of the passage from the curriculum is Science, that is how they would gain content in Spanish for that specific core content area.Same for an English day. DBN: 09X457 School: SHERIDAN ACADEMY FOR YOUNG LEADERS 154 of 232
